celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by that.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. this ﴿الْكِتَابُ﴾ which Muhammad recites ﴿لَا رَيْبَ﴾ doubt ﴿فِيهِ﴾ that it is from Allah. The negated clause is the khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is ذَلِكَ, and pointing with it [i.e. with the demonstrative of the far] is for magnification. ﴿هُدًى﴾ a second khabar, i.e. guiding ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ those who are coming to taqwā (God-consciousness) by obeying the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, since by that they guard themselves against the Fire.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ who affirm as true ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ what is hidden from them: the Resurrection, the Garden and the Fire ﴿وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ i.e. perform it with all its due requirements ﴿وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ We have given them ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in obedience to Allah.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ i.e. the Torah, the Gospel and others ﴿وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ know.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ those described by what has been mentioned ﴿عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ those who attain the Garden and are saved from the Fire.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ such as Abū Jahl, Abū Lahab and their like ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ﴾ read with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second changed into an alif, with it softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, or without it ﴿أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ because Allah knows that of them; so do not hope for their belief. Inzār (warning) is informing combined with making afraid.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ He has stamped them and sealed them firmly, so no good enters them ﴿وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ﴾ i.e. its places, so they do not benefit from the truth they hear ﴿وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ﴾ a covering, so they do not see the truth ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ strong and lasting. And the following was revealed about the hypocrites:

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection, because it is the last of days ﴿وَمَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ here the meaning of مَنْ [i.e. plural] is observed, while in the pronoun of يَقُولُ its wording [i.e. singular] is observed.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ by showing the opposite of the disbelief they conceal, in order to ward off from themselves its worldly rulings ﴿وَمَا يُخَادِعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ because the evil consequence of their deception returns upon them: they are exposed in this world by Allah informing His Prophet of what they conceal, and they will be punished in the Hereafter ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ know that their deception is against themselves. The mukhādaʿa (form III, normally mutual action) here is from one party only, as in ʿāqabtu al-liṣṣ ("I punished the thief"), and mentioning Allah in it is for embellishment (taḥsīn). In one reading: [وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ].

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ doubt and hypocrisy, which sicken their hearts, i.e. weaken them ﴿فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا﴾ through the Quran He sent down, because they disbelieve in it ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ with the shadda, i.e. [they deny] the Prophet of Allah; and without it, [يَكْذِبُونَ] ("they lie"), i.e. in their saying "We believe".

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. to these ﴿لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ through disbelief and hindering from faith ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ﴾ and what we are doing is not corruption. Allah the Exalted said in reply to them:

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿أَلَا﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh) ﴿إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا كَمَا آمَنَ النَّاسُ﴾ the Companions of the Prophet ﴿قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ﴾ the ignorant, i.e. we will not do as they do. The Exalted said in reply to them: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَإِذَا لَقُوا﴾ its original form is laqiyū; the ḍamma was dropped because it is heavy, then the yāʾ because it met, being vowelless, with the wāw ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا﴾ from them and returned ﴿إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ﴾ their chiefs ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ﴾ in religion ﴿إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ at them, by outwardly showing faith.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ requites them for their mockery ﴿وَيَمُدُّهُمْ﴾ grants them respite ﴿فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ﴾ in their exceeding the limit in disbelief ﴿يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ wandering to and fro in bewilderment; it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى﴾ i.e. took it in exchange for it ﴿فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ﴾ i.e. they made no profit in it; rather they lost, because they end up in the Fire, made everlasting for them ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ﴾ in what they did.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿مَثَلُهُمْ﴾ their description in their hypocrisy ﴿كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ﴾ kindled ﴿نَارًا﴾ in darkness ﴿فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ﴾ lit up ﴿مَا حَوْلَهُ﴾ so he could see, warm himself and feel safe from what he feared ﴿ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ﴾ extinguished it; the pronoun is plural in observance of the meaning of الَّذِي ﴿وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ what is around them, bewildered as to the way, afraid. Likewise these: they felt safe by outwardly professing the word of faith, but when they die, fear and punishment come to them.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿صُمٌّ﴾ to the truth, so they do not hear it with acceptance ﴿بُكْمٌ﴾ mute as regards good, so they do not say it ﴿عُمْيٌ﴾ to the path of guidance, so they do not see it ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ from misguidance.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾ their likeness is ﴿كَصَيِّبٍ﴾ i.e. like the people caught in a rain; its original form is ṣaywib, from ṣāba yaṣūbu, i.e. to come down ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ the clouds ﴿فِيهِ﴾ i.e. in the clouds ﴿ظُلُمَاتٌ﴾ dense ﴿وَرَعْدٌ﴾ it is the angel in charge of it, and it is said: its sound ﴿وَبَرْقٌ﴾ the flashing of his whip with which he drives it ﴿يَجْعَلُونَ﴾ i.e. the people of the rain ﴿أَصَابِعَهُمْ﴾ i.e. their fingertips ﴿فِي آذَانِهِمْ مِنَ﴾ because of ﴿الصَّوَاعِقِ﴾ the intensity of the sound of thunder, so as not to hear it ﴿حَذَرَ﴾ fear of ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾ from hearing it. Likewise these: when the Quran is revealed, containing mention of disbelief, likened to darkness, and the threat against it, likened to thunder, and clear proofs, likened to lightning, they block their ears so as not to hear it and incline towards faith and leaving their religion, which to them is death. ﴿وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in knowledge and power, so they do not escape Him.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿يَكَادُ﴾ comes close ﴿الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾ takes them quickly ﴿كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ﴾ i.e. in its light ﴿وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾ stood still. This is a parable of how the proofs in the Quran disturb their hearts, and of their affirming what they hear in it that they like, and their stopping at what they dislike. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ﴾ in the sense of their hearings ﴿وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾ the outward ones, just as He took away the inward ones ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ He wills ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ and among that is taking away what has been mentioned.

celaleyn:143-143.t:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We guided you to it, ﴿جَعَلْنَاكُمْ﴾ O community of Muhammad, ﴿أُمَّةً وَسَطًا﴾ choice and upright (ʿudūl), ﴿لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, that their messengers conveyed [the message] to them, ﴿وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا﴾ that he conveyed it to you. ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا﴾ We did not make (ṣayyarnā) ﴿الْقِبْلَةَ﴾ for you now the direction ﴿الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ at first, namely the Kaaba. He ﷺ used to pray towards it; then when he emigrated he was commanded to face Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) to win over the Jews, so he prayed towards it for sixteen or seventeen months, then he was turned [back] ﴿إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ﴾ with a knowledge of manifestation (ʿilm ẓuhūr) ﴿مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ﴾ and believes him ﴿مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ﴾ i.e. returns to disbelief, doubting the religion and supposing that the Prophet ﷺ was perplexed about his affair; and a group did apostatize because of that. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy [form, inna], and its noun (ism) is omitted, i.e. "and indeed it" (wa-innahā) ﴿كَانَتْ﴾ i.e. the turning towards it ﴿لَكَبِيرَةً﴾ hard upon people ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ﴾ among them. ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ﴾ i.e. your prayer towards Bayt al-Maqdis; rather He will reward you for it, since the occasion of its revelation was the question about those who died before the change [of qibla]. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ﴾ the believers ﴿لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ in not letting their deeds go to waste. Raʾfa is intense mercy, and the more emphatic [word] was put first for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).
[Translator's note: al-Jalalayn identifies the earlier qibla «الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا» as the Kaaba, translated as written.]

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿قَدْ﴾ for affirmation (taḥqīq) ﴿نَرَى تَقَلُّبَ﴾ the turning ﴿وَجْهِكَ فِي﴾ the direction of ﴿السَّمَاءِ﴾ looking up for revelation and longing for the command to face the Kaaba. He wished for that because it was the qibla of Ibrāhīm, and because it would more likely draw the Arabs to Islam. ﴿فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ﴾ We shall surely turn you ﴿قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا﴾ that you love. ﴿فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ﴾ face, in the prayer, ﴿شَطْرَ﴾ towards ﴿الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. the Kaaba. ﴿وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ﴾ an address to the community ﴿فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ in the prayer ﴿شَطْرَهُ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the turning to the Kaaba ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ the established [truth] ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ because of what is in their books of the description of the Prophet ﷺ, that he would turn towards it. ﴿وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with tāʾ, [addressing] you believers, of your compliance with His command; and with yāʾ [يَعْمَلُونَ], i.e. the Jews, of their rejection of the matter of the qibla.

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath ﴿أَتَيْتَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ﴾ of your truthfulness in the matter of the qibla, ﴿مَا تَبِعُوا﴾ i.e. they would not follow ﴿قِبْلَتَكَ﴾ out of obstinacy; ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَتَهُمْ﴾ cutting off his hope of their accepting Islam and their hope of his returning to it; ﴿وَمَا بَعْضُهُمْ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَةَ بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. the Jews [do not follow] the qibla of the Christians, and vice versa. ﴿وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ to which they call you ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ the revelation, ﴿إِنَّكَ إِذًا﴾ if you followed them, hypothetically, ﴿لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ﴾ i.e. Muhammad ﴿كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ﴾ by his description in their books. Ibn Salām said: "I recognized him when I saw him as I recognize my son, and my knowledge of Muhammad is stronger." ﴿وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنْهُمْ لَيَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ﴾ his description ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ being ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ — this which you are upon. ﴿فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ those who doubt it, i.e. of this kind; so it is more emphatic than "do not doubt" (lā tamtari).

celaleyn:148-148.t: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ of the nations ﴿وِجْهَةٌ﴾ a qibla ﴿هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا﴾ his face in his prayer; in one reading [مُوَلَّاهَا]. ﴿فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ hasten to acts of obedience and to accepting them. ﴿أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ He will gather you on the Day of Resurrection and recompense you for your deeds. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾.

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ﴾ for a journey ﴿فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِنَّهُ لَلْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ; its like has preceded. He repeated it to make clear that the ruling for travel and otherwise is the same.

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ﴾ He repeated it for emphasis (taʾkīd). ﴿لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the Jews or the idolaters ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ﴾ i.e. disputation about turning to other than it. It came so that their disputing with you would cease, [namely] the Jews' saying, "He denies our religion yet follows our qibla," and the idolaters' saying, "He claims the creed of Ibrāhīm yet opposes his qibla." ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ﴾ through obstinacy, for they say, "He turned to it only out of inclination to the religion of his forefathers." The exception is connected (muttaṣil), and the meaning is: no one will have any talk against you except the talk of these. ﴿فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ﴾ do not fear their disputing about turning to it, ﴿وَاخْشَوْنِي﴾ by complying with My command; ﴿وَلِأُتِمَّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ» ﴿نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by guidance to the landmarks of your religion, ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ to the truth.

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُتِمَّ», i.e. a completing like the completing of it by Our sending ﴿فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا مِنْكُمْ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿يَتْلُوا عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ the Quran ﴿وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ﴾ purifies you from associating partners [with Allah] ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ the rulings in it ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿فَاذْكُرُونِي﴾ through prayer, glorification (tasbīḥ) and the like, ﴿أَذْكُرْكُمْ﴾ it is said its meaning is: I will recompense you. In the hadith from Allah: "Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than his gathering." ﴿وَاشْكُرُوا لِي﴾ My blessing, through obedience, ﴿وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ﴾ through disobedience.

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَعِينُوا﴾ for the Hereafter ﴿بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ in obedience and affliction ﴿وَالصَّلَوةِ﴾ He singled it out for mention because of its recurrence and its greatness. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ with help.

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ "they are" ﴿أَمْوَاتٌ بَلْ﴾ they are ﴿أَحْيَاءٌ﴾ their spirits are in the crops of green birds that roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, according to a hadith to that effect; ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ you do not know the state they are in.

celaleyn:155-155.t:
﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ﴾ of the enemy ﴿وَالْجُوعِ﴾ drought ﴿وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ﴾ through destruction ﴿وَالْأَنْفُسِ﴾ through killing, death and illness ﴿وَالثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ through blights; i.e. We shall surely test you and see whether you are patient or not. ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in affliction, of Paradise. They are
[Translator's note: the entry ends with «هُمُ» ("they are"), which introduces «الَّذِينَ» at the start of the next verse as a khabar (predicate).]

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ an affliction, ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ﴾ as His possession and servants; He does with us what He wills; ﴿وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, and He will recompense us. In the hadith: "Whoever says the istirjāʿ (i.e. 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return') at a calamity, Allah rewards him for it and replaces it for him with something better." And in it [is also] that the lamp of the Prophet ﷺ went out and he said the istirjāʿ, and ʿĀʾisha said: "This is only a lamp," and he said: "Everything that grieves the believer is a calamity (muṣība)." Abū Dāwūd narrated it in his Marāsīl.

celaleyn:250-250.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا بَرَزُوا لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ﴾ that is, they came out to fight them and drew up in ranks, ﴿قَالُوا رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ﴾ pour out ﴿عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا﴾ by strengthening our hearts for the struggle (jihād) ﴿وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:251-251.t: ﴿فَهَزَمُوهُمْ﴾ they broke them ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will ﴿وَقَتَلَ دَاوُدُ﴾ — he was in the army of Ṭālūt — ﴿جَالُوتَ وَآتَاهُ﴾ that is, Dāwūd ﴿اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ﴾ over the Children of Israel ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ prophethood, after the death of Shamwīl and Ṭālūt; the two had never been combined in anyone before him ﴿وَعَلَّمَهُ مِمَّا يَشَاءُ﴾ such as the craft of making coats of mail and the speech of birds ﴿وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) of part [for the whole] from «النَّاسَ» ﴿بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ﴾ through the dominance of the idolaters, the killing of the Muslims and the destruction of the mosques ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ so He repels some of them by means of others.

celaleyn:252-252.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ that is, these verses ﴿آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا﴾ We relate them ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ in truthfulness ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:253-253.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿الرُّسُلُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ by singling him out for a distinction that no one else has ﴿مِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ such as Mūsā ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ﴾ that is, Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿دَرَجَاتٍ﴾ above the others, through the universality of his call, the sealing of prophethood, the preference of his community over all other communities, the abundant miracles and the many special qualities ﴿وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ﴾ We strengthened him ﴿بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ﴾ Jibrīl, who went with him wherever he went ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ the guidance of all people ﴿مَا اقْتَتَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ after the messengers, that is, their communities ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ because of their disagreement and their declaring one another astray ﴿وَلَكِنِ اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ because He willed that ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ﴾ stood firm in his faith ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَفَرَ﴾ such as the Christians after the Messiah ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ﴾ in granting success to whom He wills and forsaking whom He wills.

celaleyn:254-254.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ its zakāt ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لَا بَيْعٌ﴾ in it ﴿فِيهِ﴾ ransom ﴿وَلَا خُلَّةٌ﴾ friendship that benefits ﴿وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ﴾ without His permission; and that is the Day of Resurrection. In one reading: [لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ] with all three in the nominative (rafʿ). [Translator's note: the source prints «فيه» after «لا بيع» as a gloss and then again as a Quranic word glossed "ransom"; translated as written. The variant cited is also printed with the nominative, the same as the main text; the other reading has all three accusative without tanwīn (لا بيعَ فيه ولا خلةَ ولا شفاعةَ).] ﴿وَالْكَافِرُونَ﴾ in Allah, or in what was made obligatory upon them ﴿هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ because they put Allah's command in other than its proper place.

celaleyn:255-255.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ﴾ that is, there is none truly worshipped in existence ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ﴾ the everlasting ﴿الْقَيُّومُ﴾ the One who is intensive in sustaining the management of His creation ﴿لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ﴾ drowsiness ﴿وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, as creation and as servants ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي﴾ that is, no one ﴿يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ to him for it ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ that is, of creation ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ that is, of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter ﴿وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ﴾ that is, they know nothing of what He knows ﴿إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ﴾ to teach them of it, through the reports of the messengers ﴿وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ it is said: His knowledge encompasses them; it is said: His dominion; and it is said: the Footstool (kursī) itself contains them because of its immensity, on account of the hadith: "The seven heavens are, within the Kursī, only like seven dirhams thrown into a shield." ﴿وَلَا يَئُودُهُ﴾ it does not burden Him ﴿حِفْظُهُمَا﴾ that is, the heavens and the earth ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ﴾ above His creation by His overpowering might ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ the Great.

celaleyn:256-256.t: ﴿لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ﴾ to enter it ﴿قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ﴾ that is, it has become manifest through the clear signs that faith is right guidance and disbelief is error. It was revealed concerning a man of the Anṣār who had children whom he wanted to compel to accept Islam. ﴿فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ﴾ Satan, or the idols; it is used for the singular and the plural ﴿وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ﴾ he has held fast ﴿بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَى﴾ to the firm bond ﴿لَا انْفِصَامَ﴾ no breaking ﴿لَهَا وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of what is said ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of what is done.

celaleyn:257-257.t: ﴿اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ﴾ the helper ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ of disbelief ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ of faith ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمُ الطَّاغُوتُ يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ مِنَ النُّورِ إِلَى الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ The mention of "bringing out" is either as a counterpart to His saying {يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ}, or it concerns everyone among the Jews who believed in the Prophet before his mission and then disbelieved in him. ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:258-258.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ﴾ disputed with ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ﴾ because ﴿أَنْ آتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ﴾ that is, his insolence over Allah's favour drove him to that; and he was Numrūd ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from «حَاجَّ» ﴿قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾ when he said to him, "Who is your Lord to whom you call us?": ﴿رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ﴾ that is, He creates life and death in bodies ﴿قَالَ﴾ he ﴿أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ﴾ by killing and by pardoning; and he called for two men, killed one of them and left the other. When he saw that he was dull-witted, ﴿قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾ moving on to a proof clearer than it, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا﴾ you ﴿مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ﴾ he was bewildered and stunned ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ through disbelief, to the path of argument.

celaleyn:259-259.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾ have you seen ﴿كَالَّذِي﴾ the kāf is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿مَرَّ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ﴾ it was Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis); he was riding a donkey and had with him a basket of figs and a cup of juice, and he was ʿUzayr ﴿وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ﴾ fallen ﴿عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا﴾ its roofs, when Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtunaṣṣar) had destroyed it ﴿قَالَ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يُحْيِي هَذِهِ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾ out of a sense of the greatness of His power, Exalted is He ﴿فَأَمَاتَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ and kept him there ﴿مِائَةَ عَامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ﴾ brought him back to life to show him how that is done ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him ﴿كَمْ لَبِثْتَ﴾ stayed here ﴿قَالَ لَبِثْتُ يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾ because he had slept at the beginning of the day, was taken in death, and was revived at sunset, so he thought it was the day he slept ﴿قَالَ بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عَامٍ فَانْظُرْ إِلَى طَعَامِكَ﴾ the figs ﴿وَشَرَابِكَ﴾ the juice ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ it has not changed despite the length of time. As for the hāʾ: it is said to be radical, from سَانَهْتُ, and it is said to be the hāʾ of pausing (al-sakt), from سَانَيْتُ; and in one reading it is dropped. ﴿وَانْظُرْ إِلَى حِمَارِكَ﴾ how it is — and he saw it dead, its bones white and gleaming! We did that so that you may know ﴿وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً﴾ of the resurrection ﴿لِلنَّاسِ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى الْعِظَامِ﴾ of your donkey ﴿كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا﴾ We bring them to life — with ḍamma on the nūn, and it has also been read with fatḥa, from أَنْشَرَ and نَشَرَ, two dialectal usages; and in one reading [نُنْشِرُهَا] — with ḍamma, and with the zāy: We move them and raise them. [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn's commentary was written for the reading with rāʾ (نُنْشِرُهَا / نَنْشُرُهَا, "We bring them to life"), whereas the Quranic text here is printed with zāy; and the bracketed variant is printed with rāʾ although it is described as the reading with zāy (نُنْشِزُهَا, "We move them and raise them"). Translated as written.] ﴿ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا﴾ So he looked at them as they had been assembled and clothed with flesh, and the spirit was breathed into it, and it brayed. ﴿فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ﴾ that, by direct witnessing, ﴿قَالَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ with the knowledge of direct witnessing ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and in one reading [اعْلَمْ], an imperative from Allah to him.

celaleyn:260-260.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him ﴿أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ﴾ in My power to give life? He asked him, though He knew of his faith in that, so that he would answer Him with what he asked and the listeners would know his purpose. ﴿قَالَ بَلَى﴾ I believe ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ I asked You ﴿لِيَطْمَئِنَّ﴾ to become calm ﴿قَلْبِي﴾ through eyewitness added to inference ﴿قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِنَ الطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ﴾ with kasra on the ṣād and with ḍamma [فَصُرَّهُنَّ]: incline them towards you, cut them up and mix their flesh and feathers [Translator's note: the bracketed form is printed as written; the two readings are فَصِرْهُنَّ (kasra) and فَصُرْهُنَّ (ḍamma).] ﴿ثُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَلَى كُلِّ جَبَلٍ﴾ of the mountains of your land ﴿مِنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ادْعُهُنَّ﴾ to you ﴿يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا﴾ swiftly ﴿وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ nothing is beyond Him ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making. So he took a peacock, a vulture, a crow and a rooster, did with them what was mentioned, kept their heads with him and called them; the parts flew to one another until they were complete, then came to their heads.

celaleyn:261-261.t: ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ the description of the spending of ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, in obedience to Him ﴿كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ﴾ so likewise their spending is multiplied seven hundredfold ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ﴾ more than that ﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ in His bounty ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of who deserves the multiplication.

celaleyn:262-262.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ لَا يُتْبِعُونَ مَا أَنْفَقُوا مَنًّا﴾ reminding the recipient of the favour, for example by saying: "I did him good and set his affairs right" ﴿وَلَا أَذًى﴾ to him, by mentioning that to someone whom he would not want to learn of it, and the like ﴿لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ﴾ the reward of their spending ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca ﴿اعْبُدُوا﴾ affirm the oneness of ﴿رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ brought you into being when you were nothing ﴿وَ﴾ created ﴿الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ by worshipping Him, His punishment. Laʿalla is originally for hope (tarajjī), but in the speech of the Exalted it is for certainty (taḥqīq).

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ﴾ created ﴿لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial): a carpet spread out, not extremely hard or extremely soft so that settling on it would be impossible ﴿وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً﴾ a roof ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ﴾ the kinds of ﴿الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ﴾ which you eat and with which you feed your animals ﴿فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا﴾ partners in worship ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that He is the Creator and they do not create, and none can be a god except one who creates.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ﴾ doubt ﴿مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا﴾ Muhammad, of the Quran, as to whether it is from Allah ﴿فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ﴾ i.e. of what was sent down; and مِنْ is explicative (li-l-bayān), i.e. it is like it in eloquence, beauty of composition and reporting the unseen. A sūra is a portion with a beginning and an end, at least three ayahs long. ﴿وَادْعُوا شُهَدَاءَكُمْ﴾ your gods that you worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, to help you ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in that Muhammad said it of his own accord; then do that, for you are eloquent Arabs like him. And when they were unable to do that, the Exalted said:

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ what has been mentioned, because of your inability ﴿وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ that ever, because its inimitability is evident (a parenthetical clause, iʿtirāḍ) ﴿فَاتَّقُوا﴾ by believing in Allah and that it is not the speech of humans ﴿النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿وَالْحِجَارَةُ﴾ such as their idols made of it; meaning that it is extremely hot and is fuelled by what has been mentioned, not like the fire of this world, which is fuelled by firewood and the like ﴿أُعِدَّتْ﴾ made ready ﴿لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ who will be punished with it; a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause or a permanent (lāzima) ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ﴾ inform ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ believed in Allah ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ of the obligatory and supererogatory acts ﴿أَنَّ﴾ i.e. بِأَنَّ ("of the fact that") ﴿لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ gardens with trees and dwellings ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ i.e. beneath its trees and palaces ﴿الْأَنْهَارُ﴾ i.e. the waters in them; a nahr is the place in which water flows, because the water nahara-s it, i.e. digs it out, and attributing the flowing to it is figurative (majāz) ﴿كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا﴾ were fed from those gardens ﴿مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي﴾ i.e. like that which ﴿رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before it in the Garden, because its fruits resemble each other, as indicated by ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ﴾ i.e. the provision was brought to them ﴿مُتَشَابِهًا﴾ part of it resembling part in colour, while differing in taste ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ﴾ of the houris and others ﴿مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ from menstruation and every impurity ﴿وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ remaining forever; they neither perish nor leave. The following was revealed in reply to the Jews' saying, when Allah struck the parable of the fly in His words {وَإِنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ الذُّبَابُ شَيْئًا} and of the spider in His words {كَمَثَلِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ}: "What did Allah intend by mentioning these lowly things?"

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ﴾ make ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ first mafʿūl (object) ﴿مَا﴾ an indefinite noun qualified by what follows it, the second mafʿūl, i.e. any parable whatsoever; or zāʾida (redundant) to emphasise the lowliness, in which case what follows it is the second mafʿūl ﴿بَعُوضَةً﴾ the singular of baʿūḍ, which is small gnats ﴿فَمَا فَوْقَهَا﴾ i.e. bigger than it; i.e. He does not abandon setting it forth, because of the wisdom it contains ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the parable ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ firmly established, falling in its proper place ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا مَثَلًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification), i.e. by this parable. مَا is an interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkār) and is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and ذَا, in the sense of الَّذِي together with its ṣila (relative clause), is its khabar (predicate), i.e. what benefit is there in it? The Exalted said in answer to them: ﴿يُضِلُّ بِهِ﴾ i.e. by this parable ﴿كَثِيرًا﴾ away from the truth, because they disbelieve in it ﴿وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾ of the believers, because they affirm it ﴿وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾ those who depart from obedience to Him.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) ﴿يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ what He enjoined upon them in the scriptures, namely belief in Muhammad ﷺ ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ﴾ its confirmation upon them ﴿وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ﴾ such as belief in the Prophet, ties of kinship and other things; and أَنْ [with its verb] is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun of بِهِ ﴿وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ through acts of disobedience and hindering from faith ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ those described by what has been mentioned ﴿هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ because they end up in the Fire, made everlasting for them.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَ﴾ you had ﴿كُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا﴾ sperm-drops in the loins ﴿فَأَحْيَاكُمْ﴾ in the wombs and in this world, by breathing the spirit into you. The interrogative is to express astonishment at their disbelief despite the proof being established, or for rebuke ﴿ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ﴾ when your terms end ﴿ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾ by the Resurrection ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ you will be returned after the Resurrection, and He will requite you for your deeds. And He said, as a proof of the Resurrection when they denied it:

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. the earth and what is in it ﴿جَمِيعًا﴾ so that you may benefit from it and take heed ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى﴾ after creating the earth, i.e. He directed Himself ﴿إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَسَوَّاهُنَّ﴾ the pronoun refers back to السَّمَاءِ, because it has the meaning of a plural, which it comes to be; i.e. He made it, as in another ayah {فَقَضَاهُنَّ} ﴿سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ in general and in detail. Will you not then take heed that the One able to create that in the first place, which is greater than you, is able to bring you back?

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember, O Muhammad, ﴿إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً﴾ who will succeed Me in carrying out My rulings in it, and he is Adam ﴿قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا﴾ through acts of disobedience ﴿وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ﴾ sheds it by killing, as the children of the jinn did; they were on it, and when they caused corruption Allah sent the angels against them, and they drove them away to the islands and the mountains ﴿وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ﴾ engaged ﴿بِحَمْدِكَ﴾ i.e. we say "Subḥāna Allāhi wa bi-ḥamdihi" ﴿وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ﴾ we declare You free of what does not befit You; so the lām is zāʾida (redundant), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. so we are more deserving of being made successors ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ of the benefit in making Adam successor, and that among his descendants there will be the obedient and the disobedient, so justice will become manifest among them. They said: "Our Lord will not create any creation more honoured by Him than us, nor more knowledgeable, because we preceded it and have seen what it has not seen." So Allah the Exalted created Adam from the adīm of the earth, i.e. its surface, by taking a handful of it from all its colours; it was kneaded with different waters, and He fashioned him and breathed the spirit into him, and he became a sentient living being after having been inanimate.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ﴾ i.e. the names of the named things ﴿كُلَّهَا﴾ even the bowl and the little bowl, the silent breaking of wind and the little one, and the ladle, by casting knowledge of them into his heart ﴿ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the named things; in it there is taghlīb (giving precedence) to rational beings ﴿عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ﴾ to them, to silence them ﴿أَنْبِئُونِي﴾ inform Me ﴿بِأَسْمَاءِ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ named things ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in that I will not create anyone more knowledgeable than you, or that you are more deserving of the succession. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is indicated by what precedes it.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ﴾ declaring You free of being objected to ﴿لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا﴾ it ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf ﴿الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ from whose knowledge and wisdom nothing escapes.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿يَا آدَمُ أَنْبِئْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the angels ﴿بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ﴾ of the named things; so he named each thing by its name and mentioned the wise purpose for which it was created ﴿فَلَمَّا أَنْبَأَهُمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to them, rebuking ﴿أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ what is hidden in them ﴿وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ﴾ you show, namely your saying "أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا …" etc. ﴿وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ you kept secret, namely your saying: "He will not create anyone more honoured by Him than us, nor more knowledgeable."

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ﴾ a prostration of greeting, by bowing ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ﴾ he is the father of the jinn; he was among the angels ﴿أَبَى﴾ refused to prostrate ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرَ﴾ was too proud for it and said {أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ} ﴿وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in the knowledge of Allah.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun, so that something may be conjoined to it ﴿وَزَوْجُكَ﴾ Ḥawwāʾ (Eve), with the long vowel; she was created from his left rib ﴿الْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا﴾ an eating ﴿رَغَدًا﴾ ample, without restriction ﴿حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ﴾ by eating from it; it was wheat, or the vine, or something else ﴿فَتَكُونَا﴾ and so become ﴿مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disobedient.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ Iblīs; he removed them; in one reading [فَأَزَالَهُمَا], he moved them away ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ i.e. from the Garden, by saying to them: "Shall I guide you to the tree of immortality?" and he swore to them by Allah that he was a sincere adviser to them; so they ate from it ﴿فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ﴾ of bliss ﴿وَقُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا﴾ to the earth, i.e. you two together with the descendants you contain ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ some of the descendants ﴿لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾ through some of you wronging others ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ a place of settling ﴿وَمَتَاعٌ﴾ what you enjoy of its vegetation ﴿إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ the time when your terms end.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ﴾ He inspired him with them; in one reading with آدَمَ in the accusative and كَلِمَاتٌ in the nominative, i.e. they came to him. They are: "رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا" (the ayah); so he supplicated with them ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ accepted his repentance ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ﴾ towards His servants ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْهَا﴾ from the Garden ﴿جَمِيعًا﴾ He repeated it so that something may be connected to it ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) مَا ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى﴾ a book and a messenger ﴿فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدَايَ﴾ and so believed in Me and acted in obedience to Me ﴿فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, by their entering the Garden.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ Our scriptures ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ remaining forever; they neither perish nor leave.

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ﴾ forgiveness ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ grace ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ﴾ to what is right.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ children of Jacob ﴿اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ i.e. upon your forefathers: rescue from Pharaoh, the parting of the sea, shading with the clouds and other things, by giving thanks for it through obedience to Me ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي﴾ which I enjoined upon you, namely belief in Muhammad ﴿أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ﴾ which I promised you, namely the reward for it by entering the Garden ﴿وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ﴾ fear Me, in failing to fulfil it, and none other than Me.

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ﴾ two hills in Mecca ﴿مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ the landmarks of His religion; plural of shaʿīra. ﴿فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ﴾ i.e. entered into the ḥajj or the ʿumra; their root meanings are "intending" and "visiting". ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ﴾ no sin ﴿عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ﴾ in it the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated (idghām) into the ṭāʾ ﴿بِهِمَا﴾ by running (saʿy) between them seven times. It was revealed when the Muslims disliked that, because the people of the Jāhiliyya used to go round them, and on them were two idols which they would stroke. From Ibn ʿAbbās [it is reported] that the saʿy is not obligatory, because of the option conveyed by the removal of sin; al-Shāfiʿī and others said it is a pillar (rukn). He ﷺ made its obligatoriness clear by his saying, "Allah has prescribed the saʿy for you," narrated by al-Bayhaqī and others; and he said, "Begin with what Allah began with," meaning al-Ṣafā, narrated by Muslim. ﴿وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ﴾ in one reading with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and a doubled ṭāʾ, in the jussive (majzūm) [i.e. yaṭṭawwaʿ], with the tāʾ assimilated into it; ﴿خَيْرًا﴾ i.e. "with good" (bi-khayr), i.e. does what was not obligatory upon him, of ṭawāf and other things, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ﴾ of his deed by rewarding him for it, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of it. And concerning the Jews was revealed:

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ﴾ from people ﴿مَا أَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالْهُدَى﴾ such as the verse of stoning and the description of Muhammad ﷺ ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Torah, ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ He removes them far from His mercy, ﴿وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ﴾ the angels and the believers, or everything, by invoking the curse upon them.

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ turned back from that ﴿وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ their conduct ﴿وَبَيَّنُوا﴾ what they had concealed; ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ I accept their repentance, ﴿وَأَنَا التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to the believers.

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ i.e. they deserve that in this world and the Hereafter. As for «النَّاسِ», it is said: general; and it is said: the believers.

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ i.e. the curse, or the Fire which it points to; ﴿لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ granted respite for repentance or an excuse. And when they said, "Describe your Lord to us," there was revealed:

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿وَإِلَهُكُمْ﴾ the one deserving of worship from you ﴿إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ with no peer in His essence or in His attributes; ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ He is ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾.

celaleyn:164-164.t: And they asked for a sign of that, so there was revealed: ﴿إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ and the wonders in them, ﴿وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ﴾ by going and coming, increasing and decreasing, ﴿وَالْفُلْكِ﴾ the ships ﴿الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ and do not sink though laden, ﴿بِمَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ﴾ of trade and carriage, ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ rain, ﴿فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ﴾ with vegetation ﴿بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾ its dryness, ﴿وَبَثَّ﴾ and scattered and spread by it ﴿فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ﴾ because they grow through the fertility arising from it, ﴿وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ﴾ turning them south and north, hot and cold, ﴿وَالسَّحَابِ﴾ the clouds ﴿الْمُسَخَّرِ﴾ made subservient by the command of Allah the Exalted, moving wherever Allah wills, ﴿بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ without any attachment — ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ indicating His oneness, exalted is He, ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿أَنْدَادًا﴾ idols ﴿يُحِبُّونَهُمْ﴾ with veneration and submission ﴿كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. like their love for Him. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ﴾ than their love for the rivals, because they never turn away from Him in any state, whereas the disbelievers turn [from their idols] to Allah in hardship. ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى﴾ see, O Muhammad, ﴿الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ by taking rivals, ﴿إِذْ يَرَوْنَ﴾ in the active and the passive form, [i.e.] they see ﴿الْعَذَابَ﴾ — you would see a tremendous matter; and «إِذْ» is in the sense of «إِذَا» — ﴿أَنَّ﴾ i.e. because (li-anna) ﴿الْقُوَّةَ﴾ power and dominance ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ﴾. In one reading [يَرَى] with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ], and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun referring to the listener; and it is said: [the fāʿil is] «الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا», so it is in the sense of "knows" (yaʿlamu), and «أَنَّ» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects; and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْ» is omitted. The meaning is: if they knew in this world the severity of Allah's punishment, and that power belongs to Allah alone at the time they witness it, which is the Day of Resurrection, they would not have taken rivals besides Him.

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the «إِذْ» before it ﴿تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا﴾ i.e. the leaders ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا﴾ i.e. they denied having misled them, ﴿وَ﴾ [while] they have ﴿رَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تَبَرَّأَ» ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ from them ﴿الْأَسْبَابُ﴾ the ties that were between them in this world, of kinship and affection.

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً﴾ a return to the world, ﴿فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. those followed, ﴿كَمَا تَبَرَّءُوا مِنَّا﴾ today. «لَوْ» is for wishing (tamannī), and «نَتَبَرَّأَ» is its answer. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. just as He showed them the severity of His punishment and their disowning one another, ﴿يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ evil ﴿حَسَرَاتٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial): regrets ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ after entering it. And concerning those who forbade the sāʾiba camels and the like, there was revealed:

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿طَيِّبًا﴾ an emphasizing adjective (ṣifa muʾakkida), i.e. delightful; ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ﴾ the ways ﴿الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ i.e. his making things attractive; ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ of manifest enmity.

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوءِ﴾ sin ﴿وَالْفَحْشَاءِ﴾ what is foul according to the Sharia ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ such as forbidding what has not been forbidden, and other things.

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, ﴿اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ of tawḥīd and making good things lawful, ﴿قَالُوا﴾ "No, ﴿بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا﴾ found ﴿عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا﴾" of the worship of idols and forbidding the sāʾiba and baḥīra camels. The Exalted said: ﴿أَ﴾ would they follow them ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا﴾ of the matter of religion ﴿وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ to the truth? The hamza is for disapproval (inkār).

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿وَمَثَلُ﴾ the description of ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ and of the one who calls them to guidance ﴿كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ﴾ shouts ﴿بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً﴾ i.e. a sound, without understanding its meaning; i.e. in hearing the admonition and not reflecting on it they are like cattle that hear the voice of their herdsman but do not understand it. They are ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the admonition.

celaleyn:172-172.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ﴾ the lawful things of ﴿مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ for what He has made lawful for you, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:263-263.t: ﴿قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ﴾ good speech and a gracious reply to the one who asks ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ to him for his insistence ﴿خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَا أَذًى﴾ through reminders of the favour and reproaching him for asking ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ﴾ free of need of the servants' charity ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in deferring punishment from the one who reminds of favours and causes hurt.

celaleyn:264-264.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُمْ﴾ that is, their rewards ﴿بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى﴾ a nullifying ﴿كَالَّذِي﴾ that is, like the nullifying of the spending of the one who ﴿يُنْفِقُ مَالَهُ رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ﴾ showing off to them ﴿وَلَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ and he is the hypocrite ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ﴾ a smooth stone ﴿عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُ وَابِلٌ﴾ heavy rain ﴿فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدًا﴾ hard and smooth with nothing on it ﴿لَا يَقْدِرُونَ﴾ resumptive (istiʾnāf), explaining the likeness of the hypocrite who spends to be seen by people; the pronoun is plural with regard to the meaning of «الَّذِي» ﴿عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا﴾ did; that is, they will find no reward for it in the Hereafter, just as nothing of the dust that was on the smooth stone is found on it, because the rain has removed it ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:265-265.t: ﴿وَمَثَلُ﴾ the spending of ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ﴾ seeking ﴿مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ that is, an affirmation of the reward for it, unlike the hypocrites, who do not hope for it because they deny it; and «مِنْ» marks the starting point (ibtidāʾiyya) ﴿كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ﴾ a garden ﴿بِرَبْوَةٍ﴾ with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with fatḥa [بِرُبْوَةٍ]: a raised, level place [Translator's note: the bracketed form shows the ḍamma, though it follows the mention of fatḥa; printed as written.] ﴿أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ فَآتَتْ﴾ gave ﴿أُكُلَهَا﴾ with ḍamma on the kāf and with sukūn: its fruit ﴿ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾ twice what other gardens yield ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْهَا وَابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ﴾ light rain falls on it and suffices it because of its elevation. The meaning: it bears fruit and flourishes whether the rain is much or little; likewise the spending of those mentioned flourishes with Allah whether it is much or little. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ so He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:266-266.t: ﴿أَيَوَدُّ﴾ would he like ﴿أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ a garden ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ لَهُ فِيهَا﴾ fruit ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ وَ﴾ already ﴿أَصَابَهُ الْكِبَرُ﴾ so he has become too weak to earn ﴿وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ ضُعَفَاءُ﴾ small children unable to do so ﴿فَأَصَابَهَا إِعْصَارٌ﴾ a violent wind ﴿فِيهِ نَارٌ فَاحْتَرَقَتْ﴾ so he lost it when he was most in need of it, and he and his children were left helpless and bewildered, with no means. This is a likeness of the spending of one who shows off and reminds of his favours, in its vanishing and being of no benefit when he is most in need of it, in the Hereafter. The question has the sense of negation. From Ibn ʿAbbās: it concerns a man who did acts of obedience, then Satan was sent to him and he did acts of disobedience until he burned up his deeds. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He made clear what has been mentioned ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ and so take heed.

celaleyn:267-267.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْفِقُوا﴾ that is, pay zakāt ﴿مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ﴾ the good portions of ﴿مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾ of wealth ﴿وَمِمَّ﴾ and of the good portions of ﴿مَا أَخْرَجْنَا لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ of grains and fruits ﴿وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا﴾ aim at ﴿الْخَبِيثَ﴾ the inferior ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ that is, of what has been mentioned ﴿تُنْفِقُونَ﴾ it, in zakāt; a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «تَيَمَّمُوا» ﴿وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ﴾ that is, the inferior, if it were given to you for what you are owed ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ تُغْمِضُوا فِيهِ﴾ by being lenient and turning a blind eye — so how can you pay Allah's due from it? ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ﴾ free of need of your spending ﴿حَمِيدٌ﴾ praised in every state.

celaleyn:268-268.t: ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ﴾ he frightens you with it if you give charity, so that you hold back ﴿وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ﴾ stinginess and withholding zakāt ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُمْ﴾ for spending ﴿مَغْفِرَةً مِنْهُ﴾ for your sins ﴿وَفَضْلًا﴾ provision as a replacement from Him ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ in His bounty ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the one who spends.

celaleyn:269-269.t: ﴿يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ﴾ that is, beneficial knowledge that leads to action ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا﴾ because he is bound for everlasting happiness ﴿وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ﴾ in it the tāʾ, which was originally present, is assimilated (idghām) into the dhāl; it means "takes admonition" ﴿إِلَّا أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ people of intellect.

celaleyn:270-270.t: ﴿وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ﴾ whatever zakāt or charity you have paid ﴿أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ﴾ and then fulfilled ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ﴾ so He will recompense you for it ﴿وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ by withholding zakāt and vows, or by placing spending where it does not belong, in acts of disobedience to Allah ﴿مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ﴾ to protect them from His punishment.

celaleyn:271-271.t: ﴿إِنْ تُبْدُوا﴾ show openly ﴿الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾ that is, voluntary charity ﴿فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ﴾ that is, an excellent thing is showing it ﴿وَإِنْ تُخْفُوهَا﴾ keep it secret ﴿وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ than showing it and giving it to the rich. As for obligatory charity, it is better to show it so that one is followed in it and so that one is not suspected; and giving it to the poor is mandatory. ﴿وَيُكَفِّرُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn; jussive (majzūm) by conjunction with the position of «فَهُوَ», and nominative (marfūʿ) as resumptive (istiʾnāf) ﴿عَنْكُمْ مِنْ﴾ some of ﴿سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ knowing its inward as He knows its outward; nothing of it is hidden from Him. When he ﷺ was forbidden to give charity to the idolaters so that they might accept Islam, there was revealed:

celaleyn:272-272.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ﴾ that is, guiding people to enter Islam; your duty is only to convey ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to guide into it ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ wealth ﴿فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ because its reward is for them ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُونَ إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, His reward, not anything else among the goods of this world; a statement (khabar) in the sense of a prohibition ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ its recompense ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تُظْلَمُونَ﴾ you will not be shorted any of it. The two clauses are a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first.

celaleyn:273-273.t: ﴿لِلْفُقَرَاءِ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "the charities [are]" ﴿الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, they confined themselves to jihād. It was revealed about the People of the Ṣuffa, four hundred of the Muhājirūn who devoted themselves to learning the Quran and going out with the expeditions. ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا﴾ travel ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ for trade and livelihood, because jihād keeps them from it ﴿يَحْسَبُهُمُ الْجَاهِلُ﴾ of their condition ﴿أَغْنِيَاءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ﴾ that is, because of their refraining from asking and their abandoning it ﴿تَعْرِفُهُمْ﴾ O you addressed ﴿بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾ their mark, of humility and the trace of hardship ﴿لَا يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ﴾ anything, so as to importune ﴿إِلْحَافًا﴾ that is, they do not ask at all, so importuning does not occur from them; and it (ilḥāf) is insistence ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and so will recompense it.

celaleyn:274-274.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:275-275.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَا﴾ that is, take it; it is the increase in transactions involving money and foodstuffs, in quantity or in term ﴿لَا يَقُومُونَ﴾ from their graves ﴿إِلَّا﴾ with a rising ﴿كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ﴾ throws him into fits ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ﴾ madness in them; attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَقُومُونَ» ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has befallen them ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ because they ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَا﴾ in being permissible; this is a reversal of the comparison, for emphasis. So the Exalted said, refuting them: ﴿وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَا فَمَنْ جَاءَهُ﴾ reached him ﴿مَوْعِظَةٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ فَانْتَهَى﴾ from consuming it ﴿فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ﴾ before the prohibition; that is, it is not taken back from him ﴿وَأَمْرُهُ﴾ regarding pardon for him ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ﴾ to consuming it, likening it to trade in permissibility ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ﴾ i.e. eating it, since the discussion is about that, and likewise what follows it. It is what has not been slaughtered according to the Sharia; and by the Sunna there is joined to it what is cut off from a living animal, while fish and locusts are excepted from it. ﴿وَالدَّمَ﴾ i.e. that which is poured out, as in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām; ﴿وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ﴾ the flesh is singled out because it is the main thing sought, and the rest follows it; ﴿وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. slaughtered in the name of other than Him. Ihlāl is raising the voice; they used to raise it when slaughtering for their gods. ﴿فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ﴾ i.e. necessity forced him to eat something of what has been mentioned, and he ate it, ﴿غَيْرَ بَاغٍ﴾ rebelling against the Muslims ﴿وَلَا عَادٍ﴾ transgressing against them by highway robbery, ﴿فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in eating it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to His friends ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to the people of His obedience, in that He has given them latitude in this. The rebel and the transgressor are excluded, and joined to them is everyone who is disobedient by his journey, such as the runaway slave and the illegal tax-collector; so it is not lawful for them to eat any of that as long as they have not repented. Al-Shāfiʿī holds this view.

celaleyn:174-174.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ which contains the description of Muhammad — and they are the Jews — ﴿وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, which they take in exchange for it from their lowly folk, and so they do not disclose it for fear of losing it, ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ﴾ because it is where it ends up; ﴿وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ out of anger at them, ﴿وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purify them from the filth of sins, ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, which is the Fire.

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى﴾ took it in exchange for it in this world, ﴿وَالْعَذَابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ prepared for them in the Hereafter had they not concealed. ﴿فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ i.e. how intense is their endurance! It is [an expression of] making the believers wonder at their committing what brings it on without caring; otherwise, what endurance do they have?

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned of their eating the Fire and what follows it, ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ because ﴿اللَّهَ نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نَزَّلَ»; and they differed over it, in that they believed in part of it and disbelieved in part of it by concealing it. ﴿وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ in that way — and they are the Jews; and it is said: the idolaters, concerning the Quran, since some of them said "poetry", some "sorcery" and some "soothsaying" — ﴿لَفِي شِقَاقٍ﴾ discord ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ from the truth.

celaleyn:177-177.t: ﴿لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ in the prayer ﴿قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ﴾ — it was revealed in refutation of the Jews and the Christians, since they claimed that — ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ﴾ i.e. the one possessing righteousness; and it has been read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "the righteous one" (al-barr), ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ﴾ i.e. the Books, ﴿وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَى﴾ with ﴿حُبِّهِ﴾ for it ﴿ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ kinship ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the traveller ﴿وَالسَّائِلِينَ﴾ those who ask ﴿وَفِي﴾ freeing ﴿الرِّقَابِ﴾ slaves under manumission contract (mukātab) and captives, ﴿وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَوةَ﴾ the obligatory one, while what precedes it concerns voluntary [giving]; ﴿وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا﴾ Allah or people; ﴿وَالصَّابِرِينَ﴾ accusative (manṣūb) for praise (ʿalā al-madḥ) ﴿فِي الْبَأْسَاءِ﴾ extreme poverty ﴿وَالضَّرَّاءِ﴾ illness ﴿وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ﴾ at the time of intense fighting in the way of Allah. ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ those described with what has been mentioned ﴿الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا﴾ in their faith or in claiming righteousness, ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾ [of] Allah.

celaleyn:178-178.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ﴾ is prescribed ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ﴾ equivalence ﴿فِي الْقَتْلَى﴾ in status and in act. ﴿الْحُرُّ﴾ is killed ﴿بِالْحُرِّ﴾ and is not killed for a slave, ﴿وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ وَالْأُنْثَى بِالْأُنْثَى﴾. The Sunna has made clear that the male is killed for her, and that equivalence in religion is considered, so a Muslim, even a slave, is not killed for a disbeliever, even a free one. ﴿فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ﴾ of the killers ﴿مِنْ﴾ the blood of ﴿أَخِيهِ﴾ the slain ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ in that retaliation against him is abandoned. The indefiniteness of «شَيْءٌ» conveys that retaliation lapses by pardoning part of it, and by [the pardon of] some of the heirs. In the mention of «أَخِيهِ» there is a tenderness that invites pardon, and an intimation that killing does not sever the brotherhood of faith. «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), conditional or relative, and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿فَاتِّبَاعٌ﴾ i.e. the one who pardons is to follow up the killer ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ by demanding the blood-money (diya) from him without harshness. Making the following-up consequent upon the pardon conveys that what is obligatory is one of the two; this is one of al-Shāfiʿī's two views. The second is that what is obligatory is retaliation and the diya is a substitute for it, so if he pardoned and did not name it, there is nothing [owed]; and this was declared preferable. ﴿وَ﴾ upon the killer is ﴿أَدَاءٌ﴾ of the diya ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. to the one who pardons, who is the heir, ﴿بِإِحْسَانٍ﴾ without delay or shortfall. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the stated ruling, of the permissibility of retaliation and of pardoning it in return for the diya, ﴿تَخْفِيفٌ﴾ an easing ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ for you ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ to you, since He gave latitude in this and did not make one of them binding, as He made retaliation binding on the Jews and the diya on the Christians. ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى﴾ wronged the killer by killing him ﴿بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the pardon, ﴿فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, in the Hereafter by the Fire, or in this world by being killed.

celaleyn:179-179.t: ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ حَيَاةٌ﴾ i.e. great survival, ﴿يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ possessors of intellect, because when the killer knows that he will be killed he is deterred, and so he preserves his own life and that of the one he wished to kill; so it was legislated ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ killing, for fear of retaliation (qawad).

celaleyn:180-180.t: ﴿كُتِبَ﴾ is prescribed ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ i.e. its causes, ﴿إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرًا﴾ wealth, ﴿الْوَصِيَّةُ﴾ nominative (marfūʿ) by «كُتِبَ», and [it is] what «إِذَا» is attached to — if it is adverbial (ẓarfiyya) — and indicates its apodosis — if it is conditional — and [it indicates] the apodosis of «إِنْ», i.e. "then let him make a bequest", ﴿لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ with justice, by not exceeding a third and not favouring the rich; ﴿حَقًّا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasizing the content of the clause before it, ﴿عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ [of] Allah. This is abrogated by the verse of inheritance and by the hadith "No bequest for an heir," narrated by al-Tirmidhī.

celaleyn:181-181.t: ﴿فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ﴾ i.e. the bequest, whether a witness or an executor, ﴿بَعْدَ مَا سَمِعَهُ﴾ knew it, ﴿فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ﴾ i.e. of the altered bequest ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ﴾ — in it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of the testator's words ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the executor's deed, and will recompense it.

celaleyn:182-182.t: ﴿فَمَنْ خَافَ مِنْ مُوصٍ﴾ with a single and a doubled [ṣād] ﴿جَنَفًا﴾ a deviation from what is right by mistake ﴿أَوْ إِثْمًا﴾ by doing that deliberately, by exceeding a third or singling out a rich person, for example, ﴿فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ between the testator and the beneficiary by enjoining justice, ﴿فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in that. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾.

celaleyn:183-183.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ﴾ is prescribed ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ of the nations, ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ acts of disobedience, for it breaks desire, which is their origin.

celaleyn:184-184.t: ﴿أَيَّامًا﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by «الصِّيَامُ», or by an implied (muqaddar) "fast!" (ṣūmū) ﴿مَعْدُودَاتٍ﴾ i.e. few, or fixed by a known number; it is Ramadan, as will come. He made it few as an easing for those under obligation. ﴿فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ when it is present ﴿مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ﴾ i.e. travelling a journey [long enough] for shortening [the prayer], and fasting exhausted him in the two states, so he broke his fast, ﴿فَعِدَّةٌ﴾ then upon him is the number of what he broke ﴿مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ﴾ which he fasts in its place. ﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ not ﴿يُطِيقُونَهُ﴾ due to old age or an illness with no hope of recovery ﴿فِدْيَةٌ﴾ which is ﴿طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ﴾ i.e. the amount he eats in his day, which is a mudd of the staple food of the land for each day. In one reading with fidya in a genitive construct (iḍāfa) [i.e. فِدْيَةُ طَعَامِ], and it is explicative (li-l-bayān). And it is said: "not" is not implied (muqaddar); they were given the choice at the beginning of Islam between fasting and the fidya, then it was abrogated by the specification of fasting through His saying «فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ». Ibn ʿAbbās said: except for the pregnant and the nursing woman when they break the fast out of fear for the child; for it remains unabrogated in their case. ﴿فَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا﴾ by exceeding the stated amount in the fidya, ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ i.e. the voluntary act ﴿خَيْرٌ لَهُ وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ than breaking the fast and the fidya, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better for you, so do it.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَآمِنُوا بِمَا أَنْزَلْتُ﴾ of the Quran ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا مَعَكُمْ﴾ of the Torah, by agreeing with it on the oneness of God and prophethood ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍ بِهِ﴾ among the People of the Book, because those who come after you follow you, so their sin will be upon you ﴿وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا﴾ take in exchange ﴿بِآيَاتِي﴾ in your scripture concerning the description of Muhammad ﴿ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ a small compensation of this world; i.e. do not conceal them for fear of losing what you take from your common people ﴿وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ﴾ fear Me in that, and none other than Me.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا﴾ mix ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ which I sent down to you ﴿بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ which you fabricate ﴿وَ﴾ do not ﴿تَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ﴾ the description of Muhammad ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is true.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ﴾ pray with those who pray, Muhammad and his Companions. And the following was revealed about their scholars, who used to say to their Muslim relatives: "Remain firm on the religion of Muhammad, for it is the truth."

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ﴾ belief in Muhammad ﴿وَتَنْسَوْنَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ you neglect them and do not command them to it ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah, which contains the threat against words contradicting deeds ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the evil of what you do, so that you would turn back? The clause about forgetting is the locus of the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī).

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَاسْتَعِينُوا﴾ seek help in your affairs ﴿بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ restraining the soul upon what it dislikes ﴿وَالصَّلَوةِ﴾ He mentioned it separately to magnify its importance. In the ḥadīth: "Whenever a matter distressed him ﷺ he would hasten to prayer." It is said that the address is to the Jews, since greed and love of leadership held them back from faith; so they were commanded to have patience, which is fasting, because it breaks desire, and prayer, because it produces humility and removes arrogance ﴿وَإِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the prayer ﴿لَكَبِيرَةٌ﴾ heavy ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ﴾ those who are at rest in obedience.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ﴾ are certain ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُوا رَبِّهِمْ﴾ through the Resurrection ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, and He will requite them.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by giving thanks for it through obedience to Me ﴿وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. your forefathers ﴿عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the worlds of their time.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ fear ﴿يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي﴾ in which ﴿نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَلَا تُقْبَلُ﴾ with tāʾ, and with yāʾ [وَلَا يُقْبَلُ] ﴿مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ﴾ i.e. it has no intercession that might be accepted: "فَمَا لَنَا مِنْ شَافِعِينَ" ﴿وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ﴾ ransom ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ﴾ i.e. your forefathers. The address in this and what follows is to those living in the time of our Prophet, concerning what He bestowed on their forefathers, to remind them of the favour of Allah the Exalted so that they might believe ﴿مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾ making you taste ﴿سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ the severest of it; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ ﴿يُذَبِّحُونَ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of what precedes it ﴿أَبْنَاءَكُمْ﴾ the newborn ﴿وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ﴾ keep alive ﴿نِسَاءَكُمْ﴾ because some soothsayers told him that a child to be born among the Children of Israel would be the cause of the end of his kingdom ﴿وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ﴾ punishment, or rescue ﴿بَلَاءٌ﴾ a trial, or a favour ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ فَرَقْنَا﴾ split ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ because of you ﴿الْبَحْرَ﴾ so that you entered it fleeing from your enemy ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ﴾ from drowning ﴿وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ his people along with him ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ at the sea closing over them.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا﴾ with an alif and without it ﴿مُوسَى أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ at the end of which We would give him the Torah for you to act upon ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ which al-Sāmirī cast for you, as a god ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ i.e. after his going to Our appointment ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ by taking it, since you put worship in other than its proper place.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنْكُمْ﴾ We erased your sins ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ taking ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Our favour upon you.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿وَالْفُرْقَانَ﴾ an explanatory conjunction (ʿaṭf tafsīr), i.e. that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, the lawful and the unlawful ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ by it, from misguidance.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ who worshipped the calf ﴿يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ your Creator, from worshipping it ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ i.e. let the innocent among you kill the guilty ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ killing ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ So He enabled you to do that and sent upon you a black cloud so that none of you could see another and take pity on him, until about seventy thousand of you had been killed ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ accepted your repentance ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ﴾ when you had gone out with Moses to apologise to Allah for worshipping the calf, and had heard His speech ﴿يَا مُوسَى لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ openly, with our eyes ﴿فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ﴾ the shout, and you died ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ at what befell you.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُمْ﴾ We brought you back to life ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Our favour in that.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ﴾ We screened you with thin cloud from the heat of the sun in the wilderness (al-tīh) ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in it ﴿الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى﴾ they are taranjabīn (manna-sap) and the quail (al-sumānā), with the mīm unstressed and the short final vowel. And We said: ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ and do not store it up; but they were ungrateful for the favour and stored it up, so it was cut off from them ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا﴾ by that ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ because its evil consequence falls upon them.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْنَا﴾ to them after they came out of the wilderness ﴿ادْخُلُوا هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), or Jericho ﴿فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا﴾ ample, without restriction ﴿وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ﴾ i.e. its gate ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ bowing ﴿وَقُولُوا﴾ our request is ﴿حِطَّةٌ﴾ i.e. that You remove our sins from us ﴿نَغْفِرْ﴾ and in a reading with yāʾ and with tāʾ, in both cases passive ﴿لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ through obedience, in reward.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ among them ﴿قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾ they said: "A grain in a hair", and they entered shuffling on their backsides ﴿فَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ in it an overt noun is put in place of a pronoun, to intensify the ugliness of their state ﴿رِجْزًا﴾ a punishment: plague ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾ because of their fisq, i.e. their departing from obedience; and seventy thousand of them, or fewer, perished in one hour.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذِ اسْتَسْقَى مُوسَى﴾ i.e. asked for water ﴿لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ when they were thirsty in the wilderness ﴿فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ﴾ it is the one that ran off with his garment, light, square, like a man's head, of marble or soft white stone (kaddhān); so he struck it ﴿فَانْفَجَرَتْ﴾ split open and flowed ﴿مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا﴾ according to the number of the tribes ﴿قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ﴾ tribe among them ﴿مَشْرَبَهُمْ﴾ their place of drinking, so that no others shared it with them. And We said to them: ﴿كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِنْ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) that emphasises its governing word (ʿāmil); from ʿathiya, with kasra on the thāʾ, meaning "he caused corruption".

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَى لَنْ نَصْبِرَ عَلَى طَعَامٍ﴾ i.e. one kind of it ﴿وَاحِدٍ﴾ which is the manna and quails ﴿فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا﴾ something ﴿مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْ﴾ explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا﴾ its wheat ﴿وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ﴾ Moses to them ﴿أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَى﴾ baser ﴿بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ﴾ nobler, i.e. will you take it in its place? The hamza is for disapproval (inkār). They refused to turn back, so he supplicated to Allah the Exalted, and the Exalted said: ﴿اهْبِطُوا﴾ go down ﴿مِصْرًا﴾ any of the cities ﴿فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ﴾ in it ﴿مَا سَأَلْتُمْ﴾ of plants ﴿وَضُرِبَتْ﴾ were placed ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ﴾ abasement and contempt ﴿وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ﴾ i.e. the mark of poverty, namely stillness and disgrace; so it clings to them, even if they are rich, as a minted dirham clings to its die-stamp ﴿وَبَاءُوا﴾ returned ﴿بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the placing and the wrath ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. because they ﴿كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ such as Zechariah and John ﴿بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ﴾ i.e. unjustly ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾ exceed the limit in acts of disobedience; He repeated it for emphasis (taʾkīd).

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in the prophets before ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ they are the Jews ﴿وَالنَّصَارَى وَالصَّابِئِينَ﴾ a group of the Jews or the Christians ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ﴾ among them ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ in the time of our Prophet ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ according to his law ﴿فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ﴾ i.e. the reward of their deeds ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ In the pronoun of آمَنَ and عَمِلَ the wording of مَنْ is observed, and in what follows it its meaning.

celaleyn:276-276.t: ﴿يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا﴾ He diminishes it and removes its blessing ﴿وَيُرْبِي الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾ He increases them, makes them grow and multiplies their reward ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ﴾ by declaring usury (ribā) lawful ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ wicked in consuming it; that is, He will punish him.

celaleyn:277-277.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَوةَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:278-278.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَذَرُوا﴾ abandon ﴿مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truthful in your faith, for it is the way of the believer to comply with the command of Allah the Exalted. It was revealed when one of the Companions, after the prohibition, demanded what he had been owed before. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «طالب بعض الصحابة بعد النهي كان له قبل»; the object, presumably «بِرِبًا» ("usury"), seems to have dropped out; translated according to the evident sense.]

celaleyn:279-279.t: ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ what you were commanded ﴿فَأْذَنُوا﴾ know ﴿بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ against you. In it is a severe threat to them; and when it was revealed they said: "We have no power to fight Him." ﴿وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ﴾ turned back from it ﴿فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ﴾ the principal sums of ﴿أَمْوَالِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ﴾ by taking more ﴿وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ﴾ by receiving less.

celaleyn:280-280.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ﴾ there happens to be a debtor ﴿ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ﴾ for him; that is, it is upon you to defer him ﴿إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾ with fatḥa on the sīn and with ḍamma; that is, a time of ease ﴿وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا﴾ with doubling (tashdīd), by assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ, which was originally present, into the ṣād, and without doubling, by dropping it [وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا]; that is, give charity to the one in hardship by releasing him from the debt [Translator's note: the bracketed variant is printed with tashdīd, the same as the main text; the light reading is تَصَدَقُوا.] ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better, then do it. In the hadith: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship or remits [the debt] for him, Allah will shade him in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His shade." Narrated by Muslim.

celaleyn:281-281.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ in the passive: you will be returned; and in the active: you will go ﴿فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection ﴿ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى﴾ in it ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ the recompense of ﴿مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ what it did of good and evil ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ by the reduction of a good deed or the addition of an evil deed.
