celaleyn:282-282.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا تَدَايَنْتُمْ﴾ transact with one another ﴿بِدَيْنٍ﴾ such as a forward sale (salam) or a loan ﴿إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ known ﴿فَاكْتُبُوهُ﴾ for security and to prevent dispute ﴿وَلْيَكْتُبْ﴾ the record of the debt ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌ بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ with truth in his writing, neither adding to nor reducing the amount or the term ﴿وَلَا يَأْبَ﴾ refuse ﴿كَاتِبٌ﴾ to ﴿أَنْ يَكْتُبَ﴾ when he is called to it ﴿كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ that is, He favoured him with writing, so let him not be stingy with it; the kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَأْبَ» ﴿فَلْيَكْتُبْ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿وَلْيُمْلِلِ﴾ dictate to the scribe ﴿الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ﴾ the debt, because he is the one against whom testimony is given, so let him acknowledge it so that what he owes is known ﴿وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ﴾ in his dictation ﴿وَلَا يَبْخَسْ﴾ reduce ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ that is, of the due ﴿شَيْئًا فَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا﴾ a squanderer ﴿أَوْ ضَعِيفًا﴾ unable to dictate because of youth or old age ﴿أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يُمِلَّ هُوَ﴾ because of muteness, ignorance of the language or the like ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ﴾ the one in charge of his affairs: a father, an executor, a guardian or an interpreter ﴿بِالْعَدْلِ وَاسْتَشْهِدُوا﴾ call to witness over the debt ﴿شَهِيدَيْنِ﴾ two witnesses ﴿مِنْ رِجَالِكُمْ﴾ that is, adult free Muslims ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونَا﴾ that is, the two witnesses ﴿رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَامْرَأَتَانِ﴾ shall testify ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ﴾ for his religion and integrity. The number of women is because ﴿أَنْ تَضِلَّ﴾ forget ﴿إِحْدَاهُمَا﴾ the testimony, because of the deficiency of their reason and retention ﴿فَتُذَكِّرَ﴾ with the light and the doubled form [فَتُذَكِّرَ] [Translator's note: the bracketed form is printed with tashdīd, the same as the main text; the light reading is فَتُذْكِرَ.] ﴿إِحْدَاهُمَا﴾ the one who remembers ﴿الْأُخْرَى﴾ the one who forgets. The clause of reminding is what carries the reason (ʿilla), that is, "so that she may remind if she forgets"; and it [the particle] was placed on the forgetting because that is its cause. In one reading [إِنْ] with kasra, as conditional, and with تُذَكِّرُ in the nominative as resumptive (istiʾnāf), being its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَلَا يَأْبَ الشُّهَدَاءُ إِذَا مَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿دُعُوا﴾ to bear testimony and to deliver it ﴿وَلَا تَسْأَمُوا﴾ grow weary of ﴿أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ﴾ that is, the due to which you have borne witness, because that happens so often ﴿صَغِيرًا﴾ whether it be ﴿أَوْ كَبِيرًا﴾ little or much ﴿إِلَى أَجَلِهِ﴾ the time it falls due; a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «تَكْتُبُوهُ» ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ that is, writing ﴿أَقْسَطُ﴾ more just ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ﴾ that is, more helpful in establishing it, because it reminds of it ﴿وَأَدْنَى﴾ nearer to ﴿أَنْ لَا تَرْتَابُوا﴾ doubt about the amount of the due and the term ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ occur ﴿تِجَارَةٌ حَاضِرَةٌ﴾ and in one reading [تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً] in the accusative (naṣb), in which case it (kāna) is incomplete (nāqiṣa) and its noun is a pronoun referring to the transaction ﴿تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ that is, you take possession of it and there is no term in it ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ﴾ in ﴿أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا﴾ and what is meant by it is the goods traded ﴿وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ﴾ on it, for that better prevents disagreement; this and what precedes it are commands of recommendation (nadb) ﴿وَلَا يُضَارَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ﴾ the owner of the due or the one who owes it, by distortion or by refusing to testify or to write; nor shall the owner of the due harm the two of them by burdening them with what is unfitting in writing and testifying ﴿وَإِنْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ what you have been forbidden ﴿فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ﴾ a departure from obedience, attaching ﴿بِكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in His command and His prohibition ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ what is beneficial in your affairs; an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) or resumptive ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:283-283.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ﴾ that is, travelling, and you contract a debt ﴿وَلَمْ تَجِدُوا كَاتِبًا فَرِهَانٌ﴾ and in one reading [فَرُهُنٌ], plural of رَهْنٌ ﴿مَقْبُوضَةٌ﴾ by which you secure yourselves. The Sunna has made clear that pledging is permissible when resident and when a scribe is available; the restriction to what is mentioned is because security is more needed in that case. His saying «مَقْبُوضَةٌ» indicates that taking possession is a condition of the pledge, and that possession by the pledgee or his agent suffices. ﴿فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا﴾ that is, the creditor trusts the debtor with his due and takes no pledge ﴿فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ﴾ that is, the debtor ﴿أَمَانَتَهُ﴾ his debt ﴿وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ﴾ in paying it ﴿وَلَا تَكْتُمُوا الشَّهَادَةَ﴾ when you are called to give it ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْهَا فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ﴾ It is singled out for mention because it is the seat of testimony, and because when it sins the rest follows it, so he will be punished with the punishment of sinners. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ nothing of it is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:284-284.t: ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا﴾ show openly ﴿مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ of evil and resolve upon it ﴿أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ﴾ keep it secret ﴿يُحَاسِبْكُمْ﴾ inform you ﴿بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to forgive ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to punish. The two verbs are jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and nominative (marfūʿ) [فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ], that is, "then He…" [Translator's note: the Quranic text here is printed with the nominative, and the bracketed variant likewise; the jussive reading is فَيَغْفِرْ … وَيُعَذِّبْ.] ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ including calling you to account and recompensing you.

celaleyn:285-285.t: ﴿آمَنَ﴾ believed ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ Muḥammad ﴿بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ of the Quran ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to it ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ its tanwīn is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct) ﴿آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ﴾ in the plural and the singular ﴿وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ saying ﴿لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ﴾ so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others, as the Jews and Christians did ﴿وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا﴾ that is, what we were commanded, with a hearing of acceptance ﴿وَأَطَعْنَا﴾ we ask You for ﴿غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the return, through resurrection. When the verse before it was revealed, the believers complained about [involuntary] whisperings, and being called to account for them weighed on them, so there was revealed:

celaleyn:286-286.t: ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ that is, what its capacity can bear ﴿لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ of good, that is, its reward ﴿وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ﴾ of evil, that is, its burden. No one is taken to task for another's sin, nor for what he did not earn of what his soul whispered to him. Say: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾ with punishment ﴿إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا﴾ left what is right, not deliberately, as You took to task those before us for it. Allah has lifted that from this community, as has come in the hadith, so asking for it is an acknowledgement of Allah's favour. ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا﴾ a matter whose bearing is heavy on us ﴿كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا﴾ that is, the Children of Israel: killing oneself as repentance, paying a quarter of one's wealth as zakāt, and cutting out the place of impurity ﴿رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ﴾ strength ﴿لَنَا بِهِ﴾ of obligations and trials ﴿وَاعْفُ عَنَّا﴾ erase our sins ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا﴾ in mercy there is something more than forgiveness ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ our master and the one who manages our affairs ﴿فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ by establishing the proof and by victory in fighting them, for it is the way of the master to help his clients against enemies. In the hadith: "When this verse was revealed and he ﷺ recited it, it was said to him after each phrase: 'I have done so.'"

celaleyn:185-185.t: ﴿شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ﴾ from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) in it, ﴿هُدًى﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial): guiding away from misguidance ﴿لِلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ clear verses ﴿مِنَ الْهُدَى﴾ with the rulings that guide to the truth ﴿وَ﴾ of ﴿الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ with what distinguishes between truth and falsehood. ﴿فَمَنْ شَهِدَ﴾ is present ﴿مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَنْ كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ﴾ its like has preceded; it was repeated lest it be imagined to be abrogated by the generality of «مَنْ شَهِدَ». ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ﴾ and for that reason He has permitted you to break the fast in illness and travel. And because that is also in the sense of a reason for the command to fast, there was conjoined to it ﴿وَلِتُكْمِلُوا﴾ with a single and a doubled [mīm] ﴿الْعِدَّةَ﴾ i.e. the number of the Ramadan fast, ﴿وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ upon completing it ﴿عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ﴾ directed you to the landmarks of His religion, ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Allah for that. A group asked the Prophet ﷺ: "Is our Lord near, so that we may speak to Him intimately, or far, so that we must call out to Him?" So there was revealed:

celaleyn:186-186.t: ﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ﴾ to them by My knowledge, so inform them of that. ﴿أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ﴾ by granting him what he asked. ﴿فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي﴾ My call, through obedience, ﴿وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا﴾ persist in faith ﴿بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾ be guided.

celaleyn:187-187.t: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ﴾ in the sense of going in ﴿إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ﴾ through intercourse. It was revealed abrogating what was [the rule] at the beginning of Islam, of forbidding it and forbidding eating and drinking after the ʿishāʾ [prayer]. ﴿هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَهُنَّ﴾ a metonymy (kināya) for their embracing one another, or each of them needing the other. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ﴾ betray ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ through intercourse on the night of the fast — that happened to ʿUmar and others, and they apologized to the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ accepted your repentance ﴿وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ فَالْآنَ﴾ since it has been made lawful for you ﴿بَاشِرُوهُنَّ﴾ have intercourse with them ﴿وَابْتَغُوا﴾ seek ﴿مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ i.e. what He has permitted of intercourse, or decreed of offspring, ﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا﴾ the whole night ﴿حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ﴾ becomes clear ﴿لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾ i.e. the true [dawn]; an explication (bayān) of «الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ», while the explication of «الْأَسْوَدِ» is omitted, i.e. "of the night". What appears of whiteness, and what extends with it of the dimness, are likened to two threads, white and black, in their extension. ﴿ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ﴾ from dawn ﴿إِلَى اللَّيْلِ﴾ i.e. until it comes in with the setting of the sun. ﴿وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ﴾ i.e. your wives ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ﴾ residing with the intention of iʿtikāf (seclusion) ﴿فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عَاكِفُونَ»; a prohibition for one who used to go out while in iʿtikāf, have intercourse with his wife and return. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ the stated rulings ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ He set them as limits for His servants so that they stop at them, ﴿فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا﴾ more emphatic than "do not transgress them" (lā taʿtadūhā), the expression used in another verse. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ what He has forbidden.

celaleyn:188-188.t: ﴿وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ i.e. let not some of you consume the wealth of others ﴿بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ what is forbidden by the Sharia, such as theft and usurpation, ﴿وَ﴾ do not ﴿تُدْلُوا﴾ cast ﴿بِهَا﴾ i.e. its litigation, or the wealth as a bribe, ﴿إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا﴾ through litigation ﴿فَرِيقًا﴾ a portion ﴿مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ﴾ involved ﴿بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that you are in the wrong.

celaleyn:189-189.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ﴾ plural of hilāl (crescent): why does it appear thin, then increase until it is full of light, then go back to how it appeared, and not stay in one state like the sun? ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ﴾ plural of mīqāt ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ by which they know the times of their sowing, their trading, their wives' waiting periods (ʿidda), their fasting and their breaking the fast, ﴿وَالْحَجِّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «النَّاسِ», i.e. its time is known by them; for if it continued in one state, that would not be known. ﴿وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا﴾ in iḥrām, by boring an opening in them through which you enter and exit, leaving the door — they used to do that and claim it was righteousness — ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ﴾ i.e. the one possessing righteousness ﴿مَنِ اتَّقَى﴾ Allah by refraining from opposing Him. ﴿وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا﴾ in iḥrām as at other times, ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ succeed. When he ﷺ was barred from the House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya, and made a truce with the disbelievers that he would return the following year and they would vacate Mecca for him for three days, and he prepared for the ʿumra of fulfilment (ʿumrat al-qaḍāʾ), and they feared that Quraysh would not keep faith and would fight them, and the Muslims disliked fighting them in the Sanctuary, in iḥrām and in the sacred month, there was revealed:

celaleyn:190-190.t: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. to make His religion supreme ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ﴾ of the disbelievers, ﴿وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا﴾ against them by initiating the fighting. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾ those who exceed what has been set for them. This is abrogated by the verse of Barāʾa, or by His saying:

celaleyn:191-191.t: ﴿وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ find them, ﴿وَأَخْرِجُوهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَخْرَجُوكُمْ﴾ i.e. Mecca — and that was done to them in the year of the Conquest. ﴿وَالْفِتْنَةُ﴾ their associating partners [with Allah] ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ is greater ﴿مِنَ الْقَتْلِ﴾ of them in the Sanctuary or in iḥrām, which you regarded as grave. ﴿وَلَا تُقَاتِلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. in the Sanctuary ﴿حَتَّى يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِيهِ فَإِنْ قَاتَلُوكُمْ﴾ in it ﴿فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ﴾ in it. In one reading without alif in the three verbs. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ killing and expulsion ﴿جَزَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:192-192.t: ﴿فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا﴾ from disbelief and accept Islam, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:193-193.t:
﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ﴾ exist ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾ associating partners [with Allah] ﴿وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ﴾ worship ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ alone, none other being worshipped. ﴿فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا﴾ from associating partners, ﴿فَلَا تَعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — this is indicated by ﴿فَلَا عُدْوَانَ﴾ no aggression by killing or otherwise ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ and whoever desists is not a wrongdoer, so there is no aggression against him.
[Translator's note: «فَلَا تَعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ» ("then do not transgress against them") is not part of the verse; it is al-Jalalayn's implied apodosis, indicated by «فَلَا عُدْوَانَ», although the source edition marks it with Quranic brackets.]

celaleyn:194-194.t: ﴿الشَّهْرُ الْحَرَامُ﴾ the sacred [month] is in return ﴿بِالشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ so just as they fought you in it, fight them in its like — a rebuttal of the Muslims' regarding that as grave. ﴿وَالْحُرُمَاتُ﴾ plural of ḥurma: what must be respected, ﴿قِصَاصٌ﴾ i.e. like is taken in retaliation for it when it is violated. ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by fighting in the Sanctuary, in iḥrām or in the sacred month, ﴿فَاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ its requital is called aggression because it resembles in form that which it requites. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in seeking redress and refraining from aggression, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ with help and victory.

celaleyn:195-195.t: ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His obedience: jihad and other things, ﴿وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ i.e. yourselves; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), ﴿إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ﴾ destruction, by withholding spending in jihad or abandoning it, because that strengthens the enemy against you. ﴿وَأَحْسِنُوا﴾ in spending and otherwise; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ i.e. He rewards them.

celaleyn:196-196.t:
﴿وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾ perform them with their due rights. ﴿فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ﴾ are prevented from completing them by an enemy, ﴿فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ﴾ is easy ﴿مِنَ الْهَدْيِ﴾ is upon you, and it is a sheep; ﴿وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا رُءُوسَكُمْ﴾ i.e. do not leave iḥrām ﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ﴾ mentioned ﴿مَحِلَّهُ﴾ where its slaughter is lawful, which is the place of the obstruction according to al-Shāfiʿī: it is slaughtered there with the intention of leaving iḥrām and distributed among its poor, and he shaves, and by that leaving iḥrām is achieved. ﴿فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى مِنْ رَأْسِهِ﴾ such as lice or headache, and he shaved in iḥrām, ﴿فَفِدْيَةٌ﴾ is upon him ﴿مِنْ صِيَامٍ﴾ for three days ﴿أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ﴾ of three ṣāʿs of the staple food of the land to six poor people ﴿أَوْ نُسُكٍ﴾ i.e. slaughtering a sheep; «أَوْ» is for choice (takhyīr). Joined to him is one who shaves without an excuse, because he is more deserving of expiation; and likewise one who enjoys [something forbidden] other than shaving, such as perfume, clothing and oil, for an excuse or otherwise. ﴿فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ﴾ the enemy, in that it has gone or was not there, ﴿فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ﴾ enjoys ﴿بِالْعُمْرَةِ﴾ i.e. because of completing it, the things forbidden in iḥrām, ﴿إِلَى الْحَجِّ﴾ i.e. until entering iḥrām for it, provided he entered iḥrām for it [the ʿumra] in its [the ḥajj's] months, ﴿فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ﴾ is easy ﴿مِنَ الْهَدْيِ﴾ is upon him, and it is a sheep which he slaughters after entering iḥrām for it [the ḥajj]; best is the Day of Sacrifice. ﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ the offering, because it is unavailable or its price is, ﴿فَصِيَامُ﴾ i.e. upon him is the fasting of ﴿ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ﴾ i.e. while in iḥrām for it; so it is then obligatory for him to enter iḥrām before the seventh of Dhū al-Ḥijja, and best before the sixth, because fasting on the day of ʿArafa is disliked; and it is not permissible to fast them on the days of tashrīq, according to the sounder of al-Shāfiʿī's two views. ﴿وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ﴾ to your homeland, Mecca or elsewhere; and it is said: when you have finished the rites of ḥajj. In it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person. ﴿تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ﴾ a clause emphasizing what precedes it. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the stated ruling, of the obligation of the offering or fasting upon one who does tamattuʿ, ﴿لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ in that they are not within two stages (marḥala) of the Sanctuary, according to al-Shāfiʿī; if he is, there is no blood-sacrifice upon him and no fasting, even if he does tamattuʿ. In the mention of «أَهْلُهُ» there is an indication that settled residence is a condition; so if he resided [there] before the months of ḥajj without settling, or performed tamattuʿ that, then it is upon him — this is one of two opinions (wajh) in al-Shāfiʿī's school, and the second is: no. «الْأَهْلُ» is a metonymy for the self. By the Sunna, the qārin is joined to the mutamattiʿ in what has been mentioned; he is the one who enters iḥrām for the ʿumra and the ḥajj together, or adds the ḥajj onto it before the ṭawāf. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in what He commands you and forbids you, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ for one who opposes Him.
[Translator's note: the phrase «أَوْ تَمَتَّعَ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَيْهِ» appears garbled in the source; it is translated literally as "or performed tamattuʿ that, then it is upon him". The intended sense is probably "and performed tamattuʿ, then that is upon him".]

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾ your covenant to act upon what is in the Torah ﴿وَ﴾ when We had ﴿رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ﴾ the mountain; We uprooted it from its base [and held it] over you when you refused to accept it, and We said: ﴿خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with seriousness and effort ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ﴾ by acting upon it ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ the Fire, or acts of disobedience.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ you turned away ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ covenant, from obedience ﴿فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ﴾ to you, by [accepting your] repentance or delaying the punishment ﴿لَكُنْتُمْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ those who perish.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the lām of the oath (lām al-qasam) ﴿عَلِمْتُمُ﴾ you knew ﴿الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا﴾ exceeded the limit ﴿مِنْكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ﴾ by catching fish, when We had forbidden them that; they were the people of Ayla ﴿فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾ driven away; so they became them, and they perished after three days.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ i.e. that punishment ﴿نَكَالًا﴾ an example that deters from committing the like of what they did ﴿لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا﴾ i.e. for the nations of its time and after it ﴿وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ who fear Allah; they are mentioned specifically because they are the ones who benefit from it, unlike others.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ when a man of theirs had been killed and his killer was unknown, and they asked him to supplicate to Allah to make it clear to them, so he supplicated to Him ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا﴾ objects of mockery, since you answer us with something like that? ﴿قَالَ أَعُوذُ﴾ I hold back ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ from ﴿أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾ the mockers. When they knew that he was resolved,

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. what is its age ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَا فَارِضٌ﴾ old ﴿وَلَا بِكْرٌ﴾ young ﴿عَوَانٌ﴾ middle-aged ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned of the two ages ﴿فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ namely slaughtering it.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَوْنُهَا﴾ intensely yellow ﴿تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ﴾ at it, with its beauty, i.e. it impresses them.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا هِيَ﴾ is it a grazing one or a working one? ﴿إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ﴾ i.e. its kind described by what has been mentioned ﴿تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا﴾ because there are so many, so we have not found the one intended ﴿وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ﴾ to it. In the ḥadīth: "Had they not made the exception [i.e. said 'if Allah wills'], it would never have been made clear to them, to the end of time."

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَا ذَلُولٌ﴾ not broken in by work ﴿تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ﴾ turning it over for planting; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of ذَلُولٌ and falls within the negation ﴿وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ﴾ the land prepared for planting ﴿مُسَلَّمَةٌ﴾ free of defects and traces of work ﴿لَا شِيَةَ﴾ colour ﴿فِيهَا﴾ other than its own colour ﴿قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ you have spoken with complete clarity. So they sought it and found it with the young man who was dutiful to his mother, and they bought it for its hide's fill of gold ﴿فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ because of its high price. In the ḥadīth: "Had they slaughtered any cow whatsoever, it would have sufficed them, but they were hard on themselves, so Allah was hard on them."

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَادَّارَأْتُمْ﴾ in it the tāʾ is assimilated into the dāl, i.e. you disputed and pushed [the blame] onto one another ﴿فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ﴾ bringing to light ﴿مَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ about the matter. This is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ), and it is the beginning of the story.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ﴾ i.e. the slain man ﴿بِبَعْضِهَا﴾ so he was struck with its tongue or the root of its tail, and he came to life and said "So-and-so and so-and-so killed me", meaning his two cousins, and died; so they were denied the inheritance and were killed. The Exalted said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ bringing to life ﴿يُحْيِي اللَّهُ الْمَوْتَى وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ the proofs of His power ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ reflect, and so know that the One able to bring one soul to life is able to bring many souls to life, and so believe.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ O Jews, became hard against accepting the truth ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned: the bringing to life of the slain man and the signs before it ﴿فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ﴾ in hardness ﴿أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً﴾ than them ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ﴾ in it the original tāʾ is assimilated into the shīn ﴿فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ﴾ comes down from a height to below ﴿مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ while your hearts are not affected, do not soften and are not humbled ﴿وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ He only defers you until your appointed time. In one reading it is with the lower-dotted letter [i.e. يَعْمَلُونَ], and in it there is iltifāt (a shift of person) away from the second-person address.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ﴾ O believers ﴿أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ﴾ a group ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ their rabbis ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ﴾ in the Torah ﴿ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ﴾ alter it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ﴾ understood it ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they are fabricating. The hamza is for disapproval (inkār), i.e. do not hope, for they have a precedent in disbelief.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَإِذَا لَقُوا﴾ i.e. the hypocrites of the Jews ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا﴾ that Muhammad is a prophet and that he is the one foretold in our scripture ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَا﴾ returned ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ قَالُوا﴾ i.e. their chiefs who did not dissemble, to those who dissembled ﴿أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the believers ﴿بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ i.e. what He made known to you in the Torah of the description of Muhammad ﴿لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ﴾ to dispute with you; the lām is of outcome (li-l-ṣayrūra) ﴿بِهِ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter, and establish the argument against you for not following him while you know he is truthful ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that they will argue against you if you tell them, and so desist?

celaleyn:77-77.t: The Exalted said: ﴿أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), and the wāw that precedes it [i.e. that the hamza comes before] is for conjunction ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ what they hide and what they show, of that and other things, so that they would desist from that.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿أُمِّيُّونَ﴾ common people ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but rather ﴿أَمَانِيَّ﴾ lies they received from their chiefs and relied on ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not ﴿هُمْ﴾ in denying the prophethood of the Prophet and other things they invent ﴿إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ﴾ conjecture, and they have no knowledge.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ severe punishment ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الْكِتَابَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ i.e. invented by themselves ﴿ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَذَا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world. They are the Jews: they altered the description of the Prophet in the Torah, the verse of stoning and other things, and wrote them contrary to what was sent down ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لَهُمْ مِمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ of invention ﴿وَوَيْلٌ لَهُمْ مِمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ of bribes.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ when the Prophet threatened them with the Fire ﴿لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا﴾ befall us ﴿النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَةً﴾ few: forty days, the period during which their forefathers worshipped the calf; then it will end ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them, O Muhammad ﴿أَتَّخَذْتُمْ﴾ the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was dropped from it, the interrogative hamza sufficing ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَهْدًا﴾ a covenant from Him to that effect ﴿فَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللَّهُ عَهْدَهُ﴾ concerning it? No. ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather ﴿تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ it will touch you and you will abide in it forever ﴿مَنْ كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً﴾ shirk (associating partners with Allah) ﴿وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ﴾ in the singular and the plural; i.e. took hold of him and surrounded him from every side, in that he died a mushrik ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ in it the meaning of مَنْ is observed.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ in the Torah, and We said: ﴿لَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿إِلَّا اللَّهَ﴾ a declarative statement (khabar) in the sense of a prohibition; and it has been read لَا تَعْبُدُوا ﴿وَ﴾ do good ﴿بِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا﴾ dutifulness ﴿وَذِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ kinship; conjoined to الْوَالِدَيْنِ ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a speech that is ﴿حَسَنًا﴾ such as enjoining good and forbidding evil, truthfulness about Muhammad, and gentleness towards them. In one reading with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn [i.e. حُسْنًا], a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description for intensification ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ﴾ and you accepted that ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ you turned away from fulfilling it; in it there is iltifāt (a shift of person) away from the third person, and what is meant is their forefathers ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ from it, like your forefathers.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾ and We said: ﴿لَا تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَاءَكُمْ﴾ shed it by killing one another ﴿وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ﴾ none of you shall drive another out of his home ﴿ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ﴾ you accepted that covenant ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ﴾ against yourselves.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ﴾ O ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ by killing one another ﴿وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ تَظَاهَرُونَ﴾ in it the original tāʾ is assimilated into the ẓāʾ; and in one reading [تَظَاهَرُونَ] without doubling, on the basis of dropping it [Translator's note: the ayah text above is printed in the undoubled form; the base reading meant by "assimilated" is تَظَّاهَرُونَ]; you help one another ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ بِالْإِثْمِ﴾ in disobedience ﴿وَالْعُدْوَانِ﴾ wrongdoing ﴿وَإِنْ يَأْتُوكُمْ أُسَارَى﴾ in one reading [أَسْرَى] ﴿تُفَادُوهُمْ﴾ in one reading [تَفْدُوهُمْ]; you rescue them from captivity with money or otherwise, and that is among what was enjoined upon them ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) ﴿مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ﴾ connected with His words وَتُخْرِجُونَ, and the clause between them is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ); i.e. just as abandoning the ransom was forbidden. Qurayẓa had allied themselves with al-Aws, and al-Naḍīr with al-Khazraj, and each group would fight alongside its allies, ruin the others' homes and drive them out; then when they were taken captive they would ransom them. When they were asked, "Why do you fight them and then ransom them?" they would say, "We were commanded to ransom." It would be said, "Then why do you fight them?" and they would say, "Out of shame that our allies should be humiliated." The Exalted said: ﴿أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ which is the ransom ﴿وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ which is abstaining from killing, expelling and helping one another [against them] ﴿فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ﴾ contempt and abasement ﴿فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ and they were disgraced by the killing of Qurayẓa, the banishment of al-Naḍīr to Syria, and the imposition of the jizya ﴿وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَى أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ, and with tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ].

celaleyn:197-197.t:
﴿الْحَجُّ﴾ its time is ﴿أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ﴾ Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿda and ten nights of Dhū al-Ḥijja; and it is said: all of it. ﴿فَمَنْ فَرَضَ﴾ upon himself ﴿فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ﴾ by entering iḥrām for it, ﴿فَلَا رَفَثَ﴾ no intercourse in it, ﴿وَلَا فُسُوقَ﴾ acts of disobedience, ﴿وَلَا جِدَالَ﴾ quarrelling ﴿فِي الْحَجِّ﴾. In one reading [فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ] with fatḥa on the first two; and what is meant in all three is prohibition. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ such as charity ﴿يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ and He will recompense you for it. And concerning the people of Yemen — who used to perform ḥajj without provisions and so become a burden on people — there was revealed: ﴿وَتَزَوَّدُوا﴾ what will carry you through your journey; ﴿فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَى﴾ that by which one guards against begging from people and the like. ﴿وَاتَّقُونِ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ possessors of intellect.
[Translator's note: as printed, both readings show «فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ» with fatḥa; the variant meant is the one with tanwīn of ḍamma (rafathun, fusūqun) on the first two.]

celaleyn:198-198.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ﴾ in ﴿أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا﴾ seeking ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ provision ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ through trade during the ḥajj — it was revealed in rebuttal of their disliking that. ﴿فَإِذَا أَفَضْتُمْ﴾ pushed on ﴿مِنْ عَرَفَاتٍ﴾ after standing there, ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ after spending the night at Muzdalifa, with the talbiya, the tahlīl and supplication, ﴿عِنْدَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ it is a hill at the end of Muzdalifa called Quzaḥ. In the hadith, he ﷺ stood at it remembering Allah and supplicating until it became very light; narrated by Muslim. ﴿وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ﴾ to the landmarks of His religion and the rites of His ḥajj; the kāf is causal (li-l-taʿlīl). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened [from inna] ﴿كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ before His guidance ﴿لَمِنَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾.

celaleyn:199-199.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا﴾ O Quraysh, ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. from ʿArafa, by standing there with them; they used to stand at Muzdalifa, considering themselves above standing with them. «ثُمَّ» is for order in the telling (al-tartīb fī al-dhikr). ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ for your sins; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the believers ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:200-200.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ﴾ performed ﴿مَنَاسِكَكُمْ﴾ the acts of worship of your ḥajj, by having stoned Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, performed ṭawāf and settled at Minā, ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ with takbīr and praise ﴿كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَاءَكُمْ﴾ as you used to mention them on completing your ḥajj by boasting of their glories, ﴿أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًا﴾ than your mention of them. «أَشَدَّ» is accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ذِكْرًا», which is accusative by «اذْكُرُوا», since if it came after it, it would be an adjective (ṣifa) of it. ﴿فَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ رَبَّنَا آتِنَا﴾ a share ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ and he is given it there, ﴿وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ﴾ share.

celaleyn:201-201.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ blessing ﴿وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً﴾ which is Paradise, ﴿وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ﴾ by not entering it. This is an exposition of what the idolaters were upon and of the state of the believers; and the purpose of it is urging the seeking of the good of both abodes, just as He promised reward for it by His saying:

celaleyn:202-202.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ﴾ reward ﴿مِنْ﴾ on account of ﴿مَا كَسَبُوا﴾ what they did of ḥajj and supplication; ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ He reckons all creatures in the span of half a day of the days of this world, according to a hadith to that effect.

celaleyn:203-203.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ with takbīr when stoning the pillars ﴿فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُودَاتٍ﴾ i.e. the three days of tashrīq. ﴿فَمَنْ تَعَجَّلَ﴾ i.e. hastened to depart from Minā ﴿فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ i.e. on the second of the days of tashrīq, after stoning its pillars, ﴿فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ for hastening; ﴿وَمَنْ تَأَخَّرَ﴾ in it until he spent the night of the third and stoned its pillars, ﴿فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ for that; i.e. they have a choice in that. And the negation of sin is ﴿لِمَنِ اتَّقَى﴾ Allah in his ḥajj, because he is the true pilgrim. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

celaleyn:204-204.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ but does not please you in the Hereafter, because it contradicts his belief; ﴿وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ﴾ that it agrees with his words; ﴿وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصَامِ﴾ intensely hostile to you and your followers because of his enmity towards you. He is al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq; he was a hypocrite, sweet of speech to the Prophet ﷺ, swearing that he believed in him and loved him, and so he would draw near in his assembly; but Allah gave him the lie in that. He passed by crops and donkeys belonging to some Muslims and burned the former and hamstrung the latter by night, as the Exalted said:

celaleyn:205-205.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تَوَلَّى﴾ turns away from you, ﴿سَعَى﴾ goes about ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ﴾ as part of the corruption; ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَسَادَ﴾ i.e. He is not pleased with it.

celaleyn:206-206.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ in your conduct, ﴿أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ﴾ disdain and zealotry drive him to act ﴿بِالْإِثْمِ﴾ which he was commanded to guard against. ﴿فَحَسْبُهُ﴾ sufficient for him is ﴿جَهَنَّمُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ﴾ the bed — it is.

celaleyn:207-207.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْرِي﴾ sells ﴿نَفْسَهُ﴾ i.e. expends it in obedience to Allah, ﴿ابْتِغَاءَ﴾ seeking ﴿مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ His pleasure. He is Ṣuhayb: when the idolaters harmed him he emigrated to Medina and left his wealth to them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ in that He directed them to what contains His pleasure. And concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, when they venerated the Sabbath and disliked camels [i.e. their meat] after [accepting] Islam, there was revealed:

celaleyn:208-208.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the sīn [السَّلْمِ]: Islam, ﴿كَافَّةً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السِّلْمِ», i.e. in all its laws; ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ﴾ the ways ﴿الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ i.e. his making things attractive through division; ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ of manifest enmity.

celaleyn:209-209.t: ﴿فَإِنْ زَلَلْتُمْ﴾ swerve from entering into all of it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the clear proofs that it is the truth, ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ nothing prevents Him from taking vengeance on you, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:210-210.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ [i.e.] mā (not) ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ do those who refrain from entering it wait ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. His command, as in His saying «أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ», i.e. His punishment, ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍ﴾ plural of ẓulla ﴿مِنَ الْغَمَامِ﴾ clouds ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ the matter of their destruction is completed; ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ﴾ in the passive and the active form, in the Hereafter, and He will recompense.

celaleyn:211-211.t: ﴿سَلْ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ by way of rebuke, ﴿كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ «كَمْ» is interrogative, suspending (muʿalliqa) «سَلْ» from [governing] the second object, and it is the second of the two objects of «آتَيْنَا»; and its tamyīz (specification) is ﴿مِنْ آيَةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ manifest, such as the parting of the sea and the sending down of manna and quails; but they exchanged them for disbelief. ﴿وَمَنْ يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the signs He bestowed upon him, because they are the cause of guidance, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُ﴾ for disbelief, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ for him.

celaleyn:212-212.t: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ by false embellishment, so they loved it; ﴿وَ﴾ they ﴿يَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ for their poverty, such as Bilāl, ʿAmmār and Ṣuhayb, i.e. they mock them and lord it over them with wealth. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ associating partners [with Allah] — and they are these — ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَاللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ i.e. ample provision in the Hereafter or in this world, by giving those mocked among them possession of the wealth and persons of the mockers.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ by preferring it to it ﴿فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from it.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿وَقَفَّيْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ﴾ i.e. We made them follow, one messenger after another ﴿وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the miracles, such as reviving the dead and healing the blind and the leper ﴿وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ﴾ strengthened him ﴿بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ﴾ an annexation of the qualified noun to its quality, i.e. the holy spirit, Gabriel, on account of his purity; he went with him wherever he went. Yet you did not go straight. ﴿أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَى﴾ love ﴿أَنْفُسُكُمْ﴾ of the truth ﴿اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ you were too proud to follow it; this is the answer (jawāb) of كُلَّمَا and it is the locus of the interrogative, which is meant as a rebuke ﴿فَفَرِيقًا﴾ of them ﴿كَذَّبْتُمْ﴾ such as Jesus ﴿وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ the imperfect is to narrate a past state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍiya), i.e. you killed, such as Zechariah and John.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ to the Prophet, mockingly ﴿قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ﴾ plural of aghlaf, i.e. wrapped in coverings, so they do not take in what you say. The Exalted said: ﴿بَلْ﴾ for retraction (iḍrāb) ﴿لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ has put them far from His mercy and forsaken them so that they do not accept ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ and their not accepting is not due to any defect in their hearts ﴿فَقَلِيلًا مَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ مَا is zāʾida (redundant), to emphasise the fewness, i.e. their faith is very little.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ﴾ of the Torah; it is the Quran ﴿وَكَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ before it came ﴿يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ﴾ seeking victory ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ saying: "O Allah, grant us victory over them through the Prophet to be sent at the end of time" ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مَا عَرَفُوا﴾ of the truth, namely the sending of the Prophet ﴿كَفَرُوا بِهِ﴾ out of envy and fear for their leadership. The answer (jawāb) of the first لَمَّا is indicated by the answer of the second. ﴿فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا﴾ sold ﴿بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ i.e. their share of reward. مَا is an indefinite noun in the sense of "a thing", a tamyīz (specification) of the fāʿil (agent) of بِئْسَ, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is ﴿أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا﴾ i.e. their disbelief ﴿بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ of the Quran ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) of يَكْفُرُوا, i.e. out of envy that ﴿أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ﴾ without and with doubling [يُنْزِلَ] ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ revelation ﴿عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ for the message ﴿مِنْ عِبَادِهِ فَبَاءُوا﴾ returned ﴿بِغَضَبٍ﴾ from Allah, for their disbelief in what was sent down; the indefiniteness is for magnification ﴿عَلَى غَضَبٍ﴾ which they had earned before by neglecting the Torah and disbelieving in Jesus ﴿وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ bringing humiliation.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ the Quran and other [scriptures] ﴿قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا﴾ i.e. the Torah. The Exalted said: ﴿وَيَكْفُرُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (li-l-ḥāl) ﴿بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ﴾ other than it, or after it, namely the Quran ﴿وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿مُصَدِّقًا﴾ a second, emphatic ḥāl ﴿لِمَا مَعَهُمْ قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ i.e. did you kill ﴿أَنْبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in the Torah, when you were forbidden in it to kill them? The address is to those living in the time of our Prophet, about what their forefathers did, because they are content with it.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مُوسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ with the miracles, such as the staff, the hand and the parting of the sea ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ after his going to the appointed meeting ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ by taking it.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾ to act upon what is in the Torah ﴿وَ﴾ when We had ﴿رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ﴾ the mountain, when you refused to accept it, so that it would fall upon you, and We said: ﴿خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ with seriousness and effort ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ what you are commanded, with acceptance ﴿قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا﴾ your word ﴿وَعَصَيْنَا﴾ your command ﴿وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ i.e. love of it permeated their hearts as drink permeates ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿بِئْسَمَا﴾ a thing ﴿يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ﴾ in the Torah: the worship of the calf ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in it, as you claimed. The meaning is: you are not believers, because faith does not command the worship of the calf. What is meant is their forefathers, i.e. likewise you are not believers in the Torah, since you have denied Muhammad, and faith in it does not command denying him.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنْ كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ﴾ i.e. the Garden ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً﴾ exclusively ﴿مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ﴾ as you claimed ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ both conditions are attached to wishing for it, with the first being a restriction on the second; i.e. if you are truthful in your claim that it is yours, then whoever has it prefers it, and what leads to it is death, so wish for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَلَنْ يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ of their disbelief in the Prophet, which entails their lying ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers, and He will requite them.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَى حَيَاةٍ وَ﴾ more eager ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ who deny the Resurrection, for it, because they know that their destination is the Fire, unlike the idolaters, since they deny it ﴿يَوَدُّ﴾ wishes ﴿أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ لَوْ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in the sense of أَنْ, and together with its ṣila it is an interpreted maṣdar, the mafʿūl (object) of يَوَدُّ ﴿وَمَا هُوَ﴾ i.e. any of them ﴿بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ﴾ removing him ﴿مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ the Fire ﴿أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ﴾ the fāʿil (agent) of مُزَحْزِحِهِ, i.e. his long life ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ; and He will requite them. Ibn Ṣūriyā asked the Prophet, or ʿUmar, which of the angels brings the revelation; he said, "Gabriel." He said, "He is our enemy; he brings punishment. Had it been Michael we would have believed, because he brings fertility and peace." So the following was revealed:

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ﴾ let him die of rage ﴿فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿عَلَى قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ﴾ by the command of ﴿اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ the scriptures before it ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَبُشْرَى﴾ of the Garden ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ﴾ with kasra and with fatḥa on the jīm, without hamza, and with hamza, with yāʾ and without it ﴿وَمِيكَالَ﴾ conjoined to الْمَلَائِكَةِ, a conjunction of the particular to the general; in one reading [مِيكَائِيلَ] with hamza and yāʾ, and in another without yāʾ ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ He put it in the place of لَهُمْ ("to them") to make their state clear.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ i.e. clear, a ḥāl (circumstantial); a reply to Ibn Ṣūriyā's saying to the Prophet, "You have not brought us anything." ﴿وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَا إِلَّا الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿أَ﴾ did they disbelieve in them, ﴿وَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا﴾ Allah ﴿عَهْدًا﴾ to believe in the Prophet if he came forth, or [made a covenant with] the Prophet not to aid the idolaters against him ﴿نَبَذَهُ﴾ cast it aside ﴿فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ by breaking it; this is the answer (jawāb) of كُلَّمَا, and it is the locus of the disapproving interrogative ﴿بَلْ﴾ for transition (intiqāl) ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the Torah ﴿وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ i.e. they did not act upon what is in it, such as belief in the Messenger and other things ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what is in it, that he is a true prophet, or that it is the Book of Allah.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ conjoined to نَبَذَ ﴿مَا تَتْلُوا﴾ i.e. recited ﴿الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَى﴾ in the time of ﴿مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ of sorcery. They had buried it under his throne when his kingdom was taken from him; or they used to eavesdrop [on heaven], add lies to it and pass it on to the soothsayers, who recorded it; this spread, and it became widely held that the jinn know the unseen. So Solomon gathered the books and buried them, and when he died the devils showed people where they were; they dug them out and found sorcery in them, and said, "It was only by this that he ruled over you." So they learned it and rejected the books of their prophets. The Exalted said, clearing Solomon and refuting the Jews in their saying, "Look at Muhammad, mentioning Solomon among the prophets, when he was nothing but a sorcerer": ﴿وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ﴾ i.e. he did not practise sorcery, because it is disbelief ﴿وَلَكِنَّ﴾ with doubling and without ﴿الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ﴾ the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of كَفَرُوا ﴿وَ﴾ they teach them ﴿مَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ﴾ i.e. what the two were inspired with of sorcery; it has also been read with kasra on the lām [i.e. al-malikayn, "the two kings"]; who were ﴿بِبَابِلَ﴾ a town in the Sawād of Iraq ﴿هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ﴾ a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of الْمَلَكَيْنِ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "They were two sorcerers who taught sorcery." And it is said: two angels sent down to teach it, as a trial from Allah for people. ﴿وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿أَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَقُولَا﴾ to him, as sincere advice ﴿إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ a trial from Allah for people, to test them by teaching it; whoever learns it disbelieves, and whoever leaves it is a believer ﴿فَلَا تَكْفُرْ﴾ by learning it. If he insisted on being taught, they taught him. ﴿فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ﴾ by making each hateful to the other ﴿وَمَا هُمْ﴾ i.e. the sorcerers ﴿بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ﴾ by the sorcery ﴿مِنْ﴾ zāʾida ﴿أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will ﴿وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ and that is sorcery ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿عَلِمُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿لَمَنِ﴾ the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), suspending (muʿalliqa) what precedes it [from governing], and مَنْ is a relative noun ﴿اشْتَرَاهُ﴾ chose it, or took it in exchange for the Book of Allah ﴿مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ﴾ a share in the Garden ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ مَا﴾ a thing ﴿شَرَوْا﴾ sold ﴿بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ i.e. of those selling, i.e. their share of the Hereafter: that they learned it, since it made the Fire binding upon them ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the reality of the punishment they will come to, they would not have learned it.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ in the Prophet and the Quran ﴿وَاتَّقَوْا﴾ the punishment of Allah, by abandoning acts of disobedience to Him such as sorcery. The apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ is omitted, i.e. "they would have been rewarded", indicated by ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ reward; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the lām in it is for the oath ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate), [i.e. better] than that for which they sold themselves ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better, they would not have preferred that to it.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقُولُوا﴾ to the Prophet ﴿رَاعِنَا﴾ an imperative from murāʿāt ("having regard"). They used to say that to him, and in the language of the Jews it is an insult, from ruʿūna ("folly"); so they were delighted with that and addressed the Prophet with it, and the believers were forbidden it ﴿وَقُولُوا﴾ in its place ﴿انْظُرْنَا﴾ i.e. look at us ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ what you are commanded, with acceptance ﴿وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful; it is the Fire.

celaleyn:213-213.t: ﴿كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ upon faith, then they differed, some believing and some disbelieving; ﴿فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ to them ﴿مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ giving glad tidings of Paradise to whoever believed ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ warning whoever disbelieved of the Fire; ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of the Books ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزَلَ», ﴿لِيَحْكُمَ﴾ by it ﴿بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِيمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ of religion. ﴿وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ﴾ i.e. the religion ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ﴾ i.e. the Book, so some believed and some disbelieved, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the clear proofs of tawḥīd. «مِنْ» is attached to «اخْتَلَفَ», and it and what follows it are placed before the exception in meaning. ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ on the part of the disbelievers ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ مِنَ﴾ explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ his guidance ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the way of truth. And concerning a hardship that befell the Muslims there was revealed:

celaleyn:214-214.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ [i.e.] "rather, did" (bal a-) ﴿حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا﴾ [i.e.] lam (not) ﴿يَأْتِكُمْ مَثَلُ﴾ the like of what came to ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ of the believers, of trials, so that you endure as they endured? ﴿مَسَّتْهُمْ﴾ a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa) explaining what precedes it ﴿الْبَأْسَاءُ﴾ extreme poverty ﴿وَالضَّرَّاءُ﴾ illness ﴿وَزُلْزِلُوا﴾ they were shaken by kinds of affliction, ﴿حَتَّى يَقُولَ﴾ with the accusative and the nominative, i.e. "said", ﴿الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ finding the help slow in coming because of the extremity of the hardship upon them: ﴿مَتَى﴾ will come ﴿نَصْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ which we were promised? And they were answered from Allah: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾ its coming.

celaleyn:215-215.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ i.e. what it is that they should spend. The questioner was ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ; he was an old man with wealth, and he asked him ﷺ about what to spend and on whom to spend. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ an explication (bayān) of «مَا», covering little and much; in it is the explanation of what is spent, which is one of the two parts of the question; and He answered about the recipients, which is the other part, by His saying: ﴿فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ i.e. they are the most entitled to it. ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ spending or other, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and will recompense it.

celaleyn:216-216.t: ﴿كُتِبَ﴾ is prescribed ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ﴾ against the disbelievers, ﴿وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ﴾ disliked ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ by nature, because of its hardship. ﴿وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسَى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ﴾ because the soul inclines to desires that bring about its ruin and shuns obligations that bring about its happiness; so perhaps there is good for you in fighting — even if you dislike it — because in it there is either victory and booty or martyrdom and reward; and [perhaps there is] evil in abandoning it — even if you love that — because in it there is humiliation, poverty and deprivation of reward. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ what is good for you ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; so hasten to what He commands you. The Prophet ﷺ sent out the first of his raiding parties, under the command of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh; they fought the idolaters and killed Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī on the last day of Jumādā al-Ākhira, and it was confused for them with Rajab; so the disbelievers reproached them for violating it, and there was revealed:

celaleyn:217-217.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ the sacred [month], ﴿قِتَالٍ فِيهِ﴾ a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ﴾ grave in sin — a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); ﴿وَصَدٌّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ: preventing people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, ﴿وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ﴾ in Allah, ﴿وَ﴾ barring from ﴿الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. Mecca, ﴿وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ﴾ — and they are the Prophet ﷺ and the believers — and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater in sin ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ than fighting in it; ﴿وَالْفِتْنَةُ﴾ your associating partners [with Allah] ﴿أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ﴾ by you in it. ﴿وَلَا يَزَالُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ﴾ O believers ﴿حَتَّى﴾ so that ﴿يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ﴾ to disbelief ﴿إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا وَمَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ﴾ are nullified ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ righteous ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ so they are not counted and there is no reward for them. The restriction to dying in that state conveys that if he returned to Islam his deeds would not be nullified, so he would be rewarded for them and would not repeat them, such as the ḥajj for example; al-Shāfiʿī holds this view. ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾. And when the raiding party thought that even if they were free of sin they would get no reward, there was revealed:

celaleyn:218-218.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا﴾ left their homelands ﴿وَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ to make His religion supreme, ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ﴾ His reward; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the believers ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:219-219.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾ gambling: what is their ruling? ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿فِيهِمَا﴾ i.e. in engaging in them ﴿إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ great — and in one reading with the thāʾ [i.e. كَثِيرٌ, "much"] — because of the quarrelling, mutual abuse and obscene talk that come about through them, ﴿وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ through the pleasure and joy in wine, and gaining wealth without toil in gambling; ﴿وَإِثْمُهُمَا﴾ i.e. the harms that arise from them ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater ﴿مِنْ نَفْعِهِمَا﴾. When it was revealed, some people drank it and others abstained, until the verse of al-Māʾida forbade it. ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ i.e. what its amount is. ﴿قُلِ﴾ spend ﴿الْعَفْوَ﴾ i.e. what is surplus to need, and do not spend what you need and so ruin yourselves. In one reading it is nominative, with an implied "it is" (huwa). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. just as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:220-220.t: ﴿فِي﴾ the affair of ﴿الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ and so adopt what is most beneficial for you in both. ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتَامَى﴾ and the difficulty they meet concerning them: if they eat together with them they sin, and if they separate their wealth from their own and make food for them alone, it is a hardship. ﴿قُلْ إِصْلَاحٌ لَهُمْ﴾ in their wealth by making it grow, and your mixing [with them], is better (خَيْرٌ) than abandoning that; ﴿وَإِنْ تُخَالِطُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. mix your expenses with theirs, ﴿فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ﴾ i.e. they are your brothers in religion, and it is the way of a brother to mix with his brother; i.e. that is permitted to you. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ﴾ of their wealth by his mixing ﴿مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ﴾ of it, and will recompense each of them. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ﴾ He would have made it hard for you by forbidding mixing. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing over His affair, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:221-221.t: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا﴾ marry, O Muslims, ﴿الْمُشْرِكَاتِ﴾ i.e. disbelieving women ﴿حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ﴾ free woman — because the occasion of its revelation was the reproach of one who married a slave woman and the encouragement of him to marry a free idolatress — ﴿وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ﴾ for her beauty and her wealth. This is restricted to other than women of the Book, by the verse {وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ}. ﴿وَلَا تُنْكِحُوا﴾ give in marriage ﴿الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ i.e. disbelievers, believing women ﴿حَتَّى يُؤْمِنُوا وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ﴾ for his wealth and his good looks. ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ i.e. the people of shirk ﴿يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ﴾ by calling to the deeds that bring it about, so intermarriage with them is not fitting; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو﴾ on the tongue of His messengers ﴿إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the deeds that bring them about ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will, so responding to Him by marrying His friends is obligatory; ﴿وَيُبَيِّنُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ take heed.

celaleyn:222-222.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ﴾ i.e. menstruation or its place: what is to be done with women during it? ﴿قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى﴾ filth, or its location. ﴿فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ﴾ refrain from intercourse with them ﴿فِي الْمَحِيضِ﴾ i.e. its time or its place, ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ﴾ through intercourse ﴿حَتَّى يَطْهُرْنَ﴾ with sukūn on the ṭāʾ, and with doubling of it and of the hāʾ [i.e. yaṭṭahharna], in which the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated into the ṭāʾ; i.e. they wash after it stops. ﴿فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ فَأْتُوهُنَّ﴾ through intercourse ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ to avoid it during menstruation, namely the front (qubul), and do not go beyond it to another. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ﴾ rewards and honours ﴿التَّوَّابِينَ﴾ from sins ﴿وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ﴾ from impurities.

celaleyn:223-223.t: ﴿نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ﴾ i.e. the place where you sow offspring; ﴿فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ﴾ i.e. its place, which is the front (qubul), ﴿أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿شِئْتُمْ﴾ standing, sitting, lying, from the front or from behind. It was revealed in rebuttal of the Jews' saying: "Whoever comes to his wife in her front from the direction of her back, the child will be born cross-eyed." ﴿وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ righteous deeds, such as saying the basmala at intercourse; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in His command and prohibition, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلَاقُوهُ﴾ at the resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds; ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ who fear Him, of Paradise.

celaleyn:224-224.t: ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. swearing by Him ﴿عُرْضَةً﴾ a preventing cause ﴿لِأَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ i.e. a target for them, by swearing by Him often, ﴿أَنْ﴾ not ﴿تَبَرُّوا وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ — for an oath upon that is disliked, and breaking it is recommended (sunna), with expiation; unlike an oath to do righteousness and the like, which is obedience — ﴿وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ﴾. The meaning is: do not refrain from doing the righteousness and the like that has been mentioned when you have sworn [not to do] it; rather do it and expiate, because the occasion of its revelation was refraining from that. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your states.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿مَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ among the Arabs; conjoined to أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ, and مِنْ is explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿خَيْرٍ﴾ revelation ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ out of envy of you ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ His prophethood ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:106-106.t: When the disbelievers attacked abrogation (naskh) and said, "Muhammad commands his Companions to do something today and forbids it tomorrow", the following was revealed: ﴿مَا﴾ conditional ﴿نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ﴾ We remove its ruling, either together with its wording or not. In one reading with ḍamma on the nūn [i.e. نُنْسِخْ], from ansakha, i.e. We command you or Gabriel to abrogate it ﴿أَوْ نَنْسَأْهَا﴾ We defer it, so that We do not remove its ruling but lift its recitation, or We defer it in the Preserved Tablet. In one reading [نُنْسِهَا], without hamza, from forgetting, i.e. We cause you to forget it, i.e. We erase it from your heart. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is ﴿نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا﴾ more beneficial to the servants, in ease or in greater reward ﴿أَوْ مِثْلِهَا﴾ in obligation and reward ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and among that is abrogation and replacement. The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr).

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ He does in them whatever He wills ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مِنْ﴾ zāʾida (redundant) ﴿وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect you ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to keep His punishment from you if it comes to you. The following was revealed when the people of Mecca asked him to make it [i.e. Mecca] spacious and to turn al-Ṣafā into gold:

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَى﴾ i.e. his people asked him ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ such as their saying "Show us Allah openly" and other things ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَبَدَّلِ الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمَانِ﴾ i.e. takes it in its place, by neglecting to consider the clear signs and demanding others ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ has missed the true path; sawāʾ originally means the middle.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَوْ﴾ maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) ﴿يَرُدُّونَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِكُمْ كُفَّارًا حَسَدًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), being ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ i.e. their wicked souls drove them to it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ﴾ in the Torah ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ concerning the Prophet ﴿فَاعْفُوا﴾ them, i.e. leave them ﴿وَاصْفَحُوا﴾ turn away, and do not requite them ﴿حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ concerning them, namely fighting ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ an act of obedience, such as maintaining ties and charity ﴿تَجِدُوهُ﴾ i.e. its reward ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ and He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ هُودًا﴾ plural of hāʾid ("Jew") ﴿أَوْ نَصَارَى﴾ The Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najrān said that when they debated in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ; i.e. the Jews said, "None will enter it except the Jews", and the Christians said, "None will enter it except the Christians." ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ saying ﴿أَمَانِيُّهُمْ﴾ their vain desires ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾ your proof for that ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ others will enter the Garden: ﴿مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ﴾ i.e. submitted to His command. The face is singled out because it is the noblest of the limbs, so the rest are all the more so ﴿وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ affirming the oneness of God ﴿فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ﴾ i.e. the reward of his deeds, the Garden ﴿وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ worth considering, and they disbelieved in Jesus ﴿وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ worth considering, and they disbelieved in Moses ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ i.e. both groups ﴿يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ sent down to them; in the scripture of the Jews there is confirmation of Jesus, and in the scripture of the Christians confirmation of Moses. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these said ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. the idolaters among the Arabs and others ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of the meaning of ذَلِكَ, i.e. they said of every adherent of a religion: "They are not on anything" ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ in the matter of religion, and He will admit the one in the right to the Garden and the one in the wrong to the Fire.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ i.e. no one is more unjust ﴿مِمَّنْ مَنَعَ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ﴾ through prayer and glorification ﴿وَسَعَى فِي خَرَابِهَا﴾ by demolition or disuse. It was revealed as information about the Romans who ruined Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), or about the idolaters when they barred the Prophet ﷺ from the House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوهَا إِلَّا خَائِفِينَ﴾ a declarative statement (khabar) in the sense of a command, i.e. make them afraid through jihād, so that none of them enters it in safety ﴿لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ﴾ contempt, through killing, captivity and the jizya ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ it is the Fire. The following was revealed when the Jews attacked the abrogation of the qibla, or the performance of the supererogatory prayer on a mount while travelling, in whatever direction it faces:

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ﴾ i.e. the whole earth, because they are its two sides ﴿فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا﴾ your faces in prayer, by His command ﴿فَثَمَّ﴾ there ﴿وَجْهُ اللَّهِ﴾ His qibla with which He is pleased ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ﴾ His bounty encompasses everything ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the management of His creation.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ with wāw and without it; i.e. the Jews, the Christians, and those who claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him free of that ﴿بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants, and ownership is incompatible with begetting. He expressed it with مَا, giving precedence (taghlīb) to what is not rational ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾ obedient, each in what is required of it; in it there is taghlīb of the rational.

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ who brought them into being without any previous model ﴿وَإِذَا قَضَى﴾ willed ﴿أَمْرًا﴾ i.e. its coming into being ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ i.e. then it is. In one reading it is in the accusative [i.e. فَيَكُونَ], as the answer to the command.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why does not ﴿يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [telling us] that you are His messenger ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾ of those we have demanded, as proof of your truthfulness ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these said ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the disbelievers of past nations, to their prophets ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ of obstinacy and demanding signs ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ in disbelief and stubbornness; in it there is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ know that they are signs, and so believe; demanding a sign in addition to them is obstinacy.

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with guidance ﴿بَشِيرًا﴾ giving glad tidings of the Garden to whoever responds to it ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾ warning of the Fire whoever does not respond to it ﴿وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ the Fire, i.e. the disbelievers, why they did not believe; your duty is only to convey. In one reading تُسْأَلْ is in the jussive, as a prohibition.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿وَلَنْ تَرْضَى عَنْكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصَارَى حَتَّى تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ﴾ their religion ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. Islam ﴿هُوَ الْهُدَى﴾ and everything else is misguidance ﴿وَلَئِنِ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمُ﴾ to which they call you, hypothetically ﴿بَعْدَ الَّذِي جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ the revelation from Allah ﴿مَا لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect you ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to defend you from Him.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ﴾ i.e. they recite it as it was sent down; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and حَقَّ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq]; and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾ It was revealed about a group who came from Abyssinia and embraced Islam. ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. the Book that was given, by distorting it ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ because they end up in the Fire, made everlasting for them.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the like of it has preceded.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ fear ﴿يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي﴾ avails ﴿نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ﴾ in which ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ﴾ ransom ﴿وَلَا تَنْفَعُهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذِ ابْتَلَى﴾ tested ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ and in one reading Ibrāhām ﴿رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ﴾ with commands and prohibitions that He charged him with. It is said they are the rites of Ḥajj; and it is said: rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose, the tooth-stick, trimming the moustache, parting the hair, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision and cleaning oneself with water after relieving oneself ﴿فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ﴾ he carried them out completely ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him ﴿إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا﴾ an example in religion ﴿قَالَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ my children, make leaders ﴿قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي﴾ of leadership ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers among them; this indicates that it does reach those who are not wrongdoers.

celaleyn:225-225.t: ﴿لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ occurring ﴿فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ — it is what the tongue runs to without intending an oath, such as "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah"; there is no sin in it and no expiation — ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ i.e. what they intended of oaths, when you break them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ of what was idle ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in delaying punishment from the one who deserves it.

celaleyn:226-226.t: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ﴾ i.e. swear not to have intercourse with them, ﴿تَرَبُّصُ﴾ a waiting of ﴿أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ فَإِنْ فَاءُوا﴾ return, within it or after it, from the oath to intercourse, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them, for the harm they did the woman by the oath, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:227-227.t: ﴿وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلَاقَ﴾ i.e. resolve upon it, by not returning, then let them carry it out; ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of their words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of their resolve. The meaning is: after the waiting mentioned, they have nothing but returning or divorce.

celaleyn:228-228.t:
﴿وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ i.e. let them wait ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ from marriage ﴿ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ﴾ passing from the time of divorce; plural of qarʾ, with fatḥa on the qāf, which is purity or menstruation — two views. This is for those with whom the marriage was consummated; as for others, there is no waiting period (ʿidda) upon them, because of His saying {فَمَا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ عِدَّةٍ}; and for other than the woman past menstruation and the young girl, for their ʿidda is three months; and the pregnant, for their ʿidda is that they deliver their burden, as in Sūrat al-Ṭalāq; and slave women, for their ʿidda is two qarʾs by the Sunna. ﴿وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَنْ يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي أَرْحَامِهِنَّ﴾ of child or menstruation ﴿إِنْ كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ﴾ their husbands ﴿أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ﴾ by taking them back, even if they refuse, ﴿فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. in the waiting time, ﴿إِنْ أَرَادُوا إِصْلَاحًا﴾ between the two, not harming the woman. It is an urging to intend that, not a condition for the permissibility of taking back. This is in revocable divorce. «أَحَقُّ» has no comparative sense here, since no one other than them has any right to marry them during the ʿidda. ﴿وَلَهُنَّ﴾ over the husbands ﴿مِثْلُ الَّذِي﴾ they have ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ of rights ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia, of kind companionship, not causing harm and the like; ﴿وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ﴾ a precedence in right, in the obligation of their obeying them, because of the dowry and maintenance they have provided. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He has arranged for His creation.
[Translator's note: «وَفِي غَيْرِ الْآيِسَةِ وَالصَّغِيرَةِ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ» is translated as written; the sense is that the three-qarʾ rule excludes these two, whose ʿidda is three months.]

celaleyn:229-229.t: ﴿الطَّلَاقُ﴾ i.e. the divorcing after which one may take back ﴿مَرَّتَانِ﴾ i.e. two; ﴿فَإِمْسَاكٌ﴾ i.e. then upon you is retaining them after it by taking them back ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ without causing harm, ﴿أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ﴾ i.e. releasing them ﴿بِإِحْسَانٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ﴾ O husbands ﴿أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ of the dowries ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ when you divorce them, ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا﴾ i.e. the two spouses, ﴿أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. not fulfil the rights He has set for them. In one reading [يُخَافَا] in the passive, so «أَلَّا يُقِيمَا» is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from the pronoun in it; and it has been read with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] in the two verbs. ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ﴾ herself, of wealth, so that he divorces her; i.e. there is no blame on the husband in taking it nor on the wife in giving it. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ the stated rulings ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:230-230.t: ﴿فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا﴾ the husband, after the two, ﴿فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾ i.e. after the third divorce, ﴿حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ﴾ marries ﴿زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ﴾ and he has intercourse with her, as in the hadith narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim]. ﴿فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا﴾ i.e. the second husband, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ i.e. the wife and the first husband ﴿أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا﴾ to marriage after the end of the ʿidda, ﴿إِنْ ظَنَّا أَنْ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ وَتِلْكَ﴾ the things mentioned ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ reflect.
