celaleyn:231-231.t: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ are close to the end of their ʿidda, ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ by taking them back ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ without harm, ﴿أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ leave them until their ʿidda ends; ﴿وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ by taking back ﴿ضِرَارًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) ﴿لِتَعْتَدُوا﴾ against them by forcing them to ransom themselves and be divorced, and by prolonging the confinement. ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ﴾ by exposing it to the punishment of Allah. ﴿وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا﴾ an object of mockery, by contravening them; ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ through Islam ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ the rulings in it, ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ that you should give thanks for it by acting on it; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and nothing is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:232-232.t: ﴿وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ their ʿidda has ended, ﴿فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ an address to the guardians, i.e. do not prevent them from ﴿أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ﴾ who divorced them — because the occasion of its revelation was that the sister of Maʿqil ibn Yasār was divorced by her husband, and he wanted to take her back, but Maʿqil ibn Yasār prevented her, as al-Ḥākim narrated — ﴿إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا﴾ i.e. the husbands and the women ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the prohibition of preventing ﴿يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ because he is the one who benefits from it. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. abstaining from preventing ﴿أَزْكَى﴾ better ﴿لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ﴾ for you and for them, because of the suspicion feared for the two spouses on account of the attachment between them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ what contains benefit ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; so follow His command.

celaleyn:233-233.t: ﴿وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ﴾ i.e. let them suckle ﴿أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ﴾ two years ﴿كَامِلَيْنِ﴾ an emphasizing adjective (ṣifa muʾakkida); that is ﴿لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ﴾ and there is nothing beyond it. ﴿وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ﴾ i.e. the father ﴿رِزْقُهُنَّ﴾ feeding the mothers ﴿وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ﴾ for the suckling, when they are divorced, ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to his means. ﴿لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ its capacity. ﴿لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا﴾ i.e. because of it, by being forced to suckle it if she refuses, ﴿وَلَا﴾ is harmed ﴿مَوْلُودٌ لَهُ بِوَلَدِهِ﴾ i.e. because of it, by being burdened beyond his means. Attaching the child to each of them in the two places is to arouse compassion. ﴿وَعَلَى الْوَارِثِ﴾ i.e. the father's heir, who is the child, i.e. [it is] upon his guardian, from his wealth, ﴿مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ﴾ which is upon the father for the mother, of provision and clothing. ﴿فَإِنْ أَرَادَا﴾ i.e. the parents ﴿فِصَالًا﴾ weaning him before the two years, issuing ﴿عَنْ تَرَاضٍ﴾ agreement ﴿مِنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ﴾ between them, so that the child's benefit in it becomes clear, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ in that. ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ﴾ an address to the fathers ﴿أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ﴾ wet-nurses other than the mothers, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in it ﴿إِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ﴾ to them ﴿مَا آتَيْتُمْ﴾ i.e. what you intended to give them of the wage ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ graciously, such as with a willing heart. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ nothing of it is hidden from Him.

celaleyn:234-234.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ﴾ die ﴿مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ﴾ leave ﴿أَزْوَاجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ i.e. let them wait ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ after them, from marriage, ﴿أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا﴾ nights. This is for those not pregnant; as for the pregnant, their ʿidda is that they deliver their burden, by the verse of al-Ṭalāq; and the slave woman has half of that, by the Sunna. ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ the period of their waiting has ended, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ O guardians ﴿فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾ of adorning themselves and presenting themselves to suitors ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ knowing its inward as its outward.

celaleyn:235-235.t: ﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ﴾ hinted ﴿بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ﴾ whose husbands have died, during the ʿidda, such as a man's saying, for example, "You are indeed beautiful," "Who could find one like you?" and "Many a one desires you," ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ﴾ concealed ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ of the intention to marry them. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾ with proposals, and will not be patient about them, so He has permitted you to hint. ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾ i.e. marriage, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ i.e. what is recognized by the Sharia, of hinting; that is permitted you. ﴿وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ﴾ i.e. upon contracting it ﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ﴾ i.e. what is prescribed of the ʿidda ﴿أَجَلَهُ﴾ by its ending. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ of resolve and other things, ﴿فَاحْذَرُوهُ﴾ lest He punish you if you resolve; ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to one who is wary of Him, ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in delaying punishment from the one who deserves it.

celaleyn:236-236.t: ﴿لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ — in one reading [تُمَاسُّوهُنَّ] — i.e. have intercourse with them, ﴿أَوْ﴾ have not ﴿تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾ a dowry. «مَا» is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-verbal); i.e. there is no consequence upon you in divorcing at a time of no touching and no fixing [of dowry], whether sin or dowry; so divorce them ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾ give them something to enjoy, ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ﴾ the rich among you ﴿قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ﴾ the one of straitened provision ﴿قَدَرُهُ﴾ — this conveys that no regard is given to the wife's standing — ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ a provision ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to the Sharia; an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَتَاعًا»; ﴿حَقًّا﴾ a second adjective, or an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun), ﴿عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the obedient.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ﴾ the Kaaba ﴿مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a place of return to which they come back from every side ﴿وَأَمْنًا﴾ a place of safety for them from the oppression and raids that occur elsewhere; a man would meet his father's killer there and not provoke him ﴿وَاتَّخِذُوا﴾ O people ﴿مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ it is the stone on which he stood while building the House ﴿مُصَلًّى﴾ a place of prayer, by praying behind it the two rakʿas of ṭawāf (circumambulation). In one reading with fatḥa on the khāʾ [i.e. وَاتَّخَذُوا], as a declarative statement ﴿وَعَهِدْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ﴾ We commanded them ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ("to") ﴿طَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ﴾ of idols ﴿لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ﴾ those who stay in it ﴿وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ﴾ plural of rākiʿ and sājid: those who pray.

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا﴾ place ﴿بَلَدًا آمِنًا﴾ possessing safety. Allah answered his supplication and made it a sanctuary (ḥaram) in which no human blood is shed, no one is wronged, its game is not hunted and its fresh herbage is not cut ﴿وَارْزُقْ أَهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ and this was done by moving al-Ṭāʾif from Syria to it, when it had been barren, with no crops and no water ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from أَهْلَهُ; he singled them out in the supplication in keeping with His words "لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ" ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted ﴿وَ﴾ I will provide for ﴿مَنْ كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ﴾ with doubling and without, in this world with provision ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ for the span of his life ﴿ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ﴾ I will force him, in the Hereafter ﴿إِلَى عَذَابِ النَّارِ﴾ and he will find no escape from it ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the place of return, it is.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ﴾ the foundations, or the walls ﴿مِنَ الْبَيْتِ﴾ building it; attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَرْفَعُ ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ﴾ conjoined to إِبْرَاهِيمُ, both saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا﴾ our building ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of speech ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of action.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ﴾ submissive ﴿لَكَ وَ﴾ make ﴿مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنَا﴾ our children ﴿أُمَّةً﴾ a community ﴿مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ﴾ مِنْ is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), and he used it because of His earlier saying to him "لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ" ﴿وَأَرِنَا﴾ teach us ﴿مَنَاسِكَنَا﴾ the laws of our worship, or of our Ḥajj ﴿وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ They asked Him for repentance despite their being protected from sin, out of humility and to teach their descendants.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ﴾ i.e. the people of the House ﴿رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ from among themselves; and Allah answered his supplication with Muhammad ﷺ ﴿يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِكَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ i.e. the rulings it contains ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purify them of shirk ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ the Overpowering ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. none ﴿يَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ and so abandons it ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ﴾ is ignorant that it is created by Allah and must worship Him, or holds it cheap and debases it ﴿وَلَقَدِ اصْطَفَيْنَاهُ﴾ We chose him ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ for messengership and close friendship (khulla) ﴿وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ who have the highest ranks. And remember:

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ﴾ submit to Allah and make your religion sincerely His ﴿قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَوَصَّى﴾ in one reading [أَوْصَى] ﴿بِهَا﴾ the religion (milla) ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ﴾ his sons; he said: ﴿يَا بَنِيَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى لَكُمُ الدِّينَ﴾ the religion of Islam ﴿فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ a prohibition against abandoning Islam and a command to hold firm to it until death comes. When the Jews said to the Prophet, "Do you not know that Jacob, on the day he died, enjoined Judaism upon his sons?", the following was revealed:

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ present ﴿إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the إِذْ before it ﴿قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ after my death ﴿قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَهَكَ وَإِلَهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ﴾ Ishmael is counted among the fathers by taghlīb (giving precedence to the majority), and because a paternal uncle has the standing of a father ﴿إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا﴾ a badal from إِلَهَكَ ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ أَمْ has the sense of the hamza of disapproval (inkār), i.e. you were not present at the time of his death, so how can you attribute to him what does not befit him?

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); it points to Abraham, Jacob and their sons, and is feminine because its khabar (predicate) is feminine ﴿أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ﴾ has passed ﴿لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ of deeds, i.e. its recompense; a resumptive clause (istiʾnāf) ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾ the address is to the Jews ﴿مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ just as they will not be asked about your deeds; the clause is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of what precedes it.

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى تَهْتَدُوا﴾ أَوْ is for distribution (tafṣīl): the speakers of the first are the Jews of Medina and of the second the Christians of Najrān ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿بَلْ﴾ we follow ﴿مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيمَ: inclining away from all religions to the upright religion ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿قُولُوا﴾ an address to the believers ﴿آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا﴾ of the Quran ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ of the ten scrolls ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ﴾ his children ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى﴾ of the Torah ﴿وَعِيسَى﴾ of the Gospel ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ of scriptures and signs ﴿لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ believing in some and disbelieving in others, like the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿فَإِنْ آمَنُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews and the Christians ﴿بِمِثْلِ﴾ مِثْلِ is zāʾida (redundant) ﴿مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from believing in it ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ﴾ in opposition to you ﴿فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ O Muhammad, their opposition ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of their words ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of their states. And He did suffice him against them, through the killing of Qurayẓa, the banishment of al-Naḍīr and the imposition of the jizya on them.

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising آمَنَّا, accusative through an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. "Allah has dyed us". What is meant by it is His religion upon which He created people, because its mark shows on the one who holds it, like dye on a garment ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً﴾ a tamyīz (specification) ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ﴾ The Jews said to the Muslims: "We are the people of the first scripture, our qibla is older, and the prophets were not from the Arabs; had Muhammad been a prophet, he would have been from us." So the following was revealed:

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا﴾ do you dispute with us ﴿فِي اللَّهِ﴾ that He chose a prophet from the Arabs ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾ so it is His right to choose whomever He wills of His servants ﴿وَلَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا﴾ for which we are requited ﴿وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾ for which you are requited; so it is not unlikely that among our deeds there is something by which we deserve to be honoured ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ﴾ in religion and deeds, unlike you; so we are more entitled to be chosen. The hamza is for disapproval (inkār), and the three clauses are aḥwāl (circumstantial clauses).

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, do ﴿تَقُولُونَ﴾ with tāʾ, and with yāʾ [يَقُولُونَ] ﴿إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. Allah knows better; and He has declared Abraham free of both by His words "مَا كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا", and those mentioned with him follow him ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَتَمَ﴾ hid from people ﴿شَهَادَةً عِنْدَهُ﴾ that is ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. no one is more unjust than he. They are the Jews: they concealed Allah's testimony in the Torah to Abraham's ḥanīf faith ﴿وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a threat to them.

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ the like of it has preceded.

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ﴾ the ignorant ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the Jews and the idolaters ﴿مَا وَلَّاهُمْ﴾ what turned the Prophet ﷺ and the believers ﴿عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا﴾ facing it in prayer, namely Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). Using the sīn, which indicates the future, is part of informing about the unseen. ﴿قُلْ لِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ﴾ i.e. all directions; so He commands turning to whichever direction He wills, and there is no objecting to Him ﴿يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to guide ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the religion of Islam; i.e. and among them are you. And among them … [Translator's note: the text reads «وَمِنْهُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَمِنْهُمْ دَلَّ عَلَى هَذَا»; the second «وَمِنْهُمْ» appears superfluous. The sense is: "and among them are you", which is indicated by what follows (ayah 143).]

celaleyn:237-237.t: ﴿وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ﴾ is due to them, and the [other] half returns to you, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ يَعْفُونَ﴾ i.e. the wives, and they forgo it, ﴿أَوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ﴾ — and he is the husband — and he leaves her the whole. From Ibn ʿAbbās: [it is] the guardian, if she is under legal restriction (maḥjūra); and there is no blame in that. ﴿وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ i.e. that some of you be generous to others. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ and He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:238-238.t: ﴿حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ﴾ the five, by performing them in their times, ﴿وَالصَّلَوةِ الْوُسْطَى﴾ it is ʿaṣr, or ṣubḥ, or ẓuhr, or another — [several] views; He singled it out for mention because of its excellence. ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ in the prayer ﴿قَانِتِينَ﴾ it is said: obedient, because of his ﷺ saying, "Every qunūt in the Quran is obedience," narrated by Aḥmad and others; and it is said: silent, because of the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: "We used to talk in the prayer until it was revealed, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak," narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim].

celaleyn:239-239.t: ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ from an enemy, a flood or a wild beast, ﴿فَرِجَالًا﴾ plural of rājil, i.e. pray on foot, ﴿أَوْ رُكْبَانًا﴾ plural of rākib, i.e. however possible, facing the qibla or otherwise, and indicate the bowing and prostration by gestures. ﴿فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ﴾ from fear, ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. pray ﴿كَمَا عَلَّمَكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ before His teaching, of its obligations and its due rights. The kāf is in the sense of "like" (mithl), and «مَا» is maṣdariyya or a relative noun.

celaleyn:240-240.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ let them bequeath ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾ — in one reading nominative, i.e. "[is] upon them" — ﴿لِأَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ and let them give them ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ what they may enjoy, of maintenance and clothing, ﴿إِلَى﴾ the completion of ﴿الْحَوْلِ﴾ from their death, which they were obliged to wait out, ﴿غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. not being expelled from their dwelling. ﴿فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ﴾ of their own accord, ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ O guardians of the deceased, ﴿فِي مَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ مِنْ مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ according to the Sharia, such as adorning herself, abandoning mourning (iḥdād), and [your] cutting off maintenance from her. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making. The bequest mentioned is abrogated by the verse of inheritance, and the year's waiting by the verse {أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا}, which precedes [in the text] but is later in revelation; and lodging remains established for her according to al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.

celaleyn:241-241.t: ﴿وَلِلْمُطَلَّقَاتِ مَتَاعٌ﴾ which they are given ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ according to what is possible, ﴿حَقًّا﴾ accusative by its implied (muqaddar) verb, ﴿عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ [of] Allah the Exalted. He repeated it so that it covers the woman with whom the marriage was consummated as well, since the preceding verse is about other than her.

celaleyn:242-242.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He makes clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ reflect.

celaleyn:243-243.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ an interrogative of wonder and of arousing eagerness to hear what follows it, i.e. has your knowledge not reached ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ﴾ four, or eight, or ten, or thirty, or forty, or seventy thousand, ﴿حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose)? They were a people of the Children of Israel; the plague struck their land and they fled. ﴿فَقَالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا﴾ and they died; ﴿ثُمَّ أَحْيَاهُمْ﴾ after eight days or more, through the supplication of their prophet Ḥizqīl — with kasra on the unpointed [ḥāʾ] and on the qāf, and sukūn on the zāy — and they lived for a long time with the trace of death upon them; they would not put on a garment but it became like a shroud, and this continued among their descendants. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ and part of it is reviving these, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ — and they are the disbelievers — ﴿لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾. The purpose of mentioning the account of these is to encourage the believers to fight; and for that reason there is conjoined to it:

celaleyn:244-244.t: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. to make His religion supreme, ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of your words, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your states, and will recompense you.

celaleyn:245-245.t: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾ by spending his wealth in the way of Allah ﴿قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ by spending it for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a willing heart, ﴿فَيُضَاعِفَهُ﴾ — in one reading [فَيُضَعِّفَهُ] with doubling — ﴿لَهُ أَضْعَافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ from ten to more than seven hundred, as will come. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ﴾ withholds provision from whom He wills, as a test, ﴿وَيَبْسُطُ﴾ makes it ample for whom He wills, as a trial; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, at the resurrection, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

celaleyn:246-246.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ﴾ the group ﴿مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the death of ﴿مُوسَى﴾ i.e. to their story and their account, ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا لِنَبِيٍّ لَهُمْ﴾ he is Shamwīl (Samuel), ﴿ابْعَثْ﴾ set up ﴿لَنَا مَلِكًا نُقَاتِلْ﴾ with him ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — by whom our word will be united and to whom we will refer? ﴿قَالَ﴾ the prophet to them: ﴿هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra [on the sīn] ﴿إِنْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَاتِلُوا﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «عَسَى»; the interrogative is to affirm the expectation conveyed by it. ﴿قَالُوا وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا مِنْ دِيَارِنَا وَأَبْنَائِنَا﴾ by their being captured and killed — the people of Jālūt (Goliath) had done that to them — i.e. nothing prevents us from it while what calls for it exists. The Exalted said: ﴿فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from it and were cowardly, ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ — they are the ones who crossed the river with Ṭālūt (Saul), as will come. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ and will recompense them. The prophet asked his Lord to send a king, and He answered him by sending Ṭālūt.

celaleyn:247-247.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا قَالُوا أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ عَلَيْنَا وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْهُ﴾ because he was not from the tribe of kingship nor of prophethood, and he was a tanner or a shepherd, ﴿وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ سَعَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ﴾ with which to help himself in establishing the kingship? ﴿قَالَ﴾ the prophet to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاهُ﴾ chose him for the kingship ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ وَزَادَهُ بَسْطَةً﴾ amplitude ﴿فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ﴾ — he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel at that time, the most handsome of them and the most perfect in form. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُؤْتِي مُلْكَهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to give it to; there is no objecting to Him. ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ in His bounty, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of who is worthy of it.

celaleyn:248-248.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ﴾ when they asked him for a sign of his kingship: ﴿إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ﴾ the chest, in which were images of the prophets; Allah sent it down to Ādam and it continued down to them; then the Amalekites overpowered them for it and took it. They used to seek victory over their enemy through it, put it in front in battle, and find tranquillity in it, as the Exalted said: ﴿فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ﴾ reassurance for your hearts ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسَى وَآلُ هَارُونَ﴾ i.e. what the two of them left; it is the sandals of Mūsā and his staff, the turban of Hārūn, a qafīz (measure) of the manna that used to come down upon them, and fragments of the Tablets. ﴿تَحْمِلُهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَأْتِيَكُمُ». ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ﴾ of his kingship ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. So the angels carried it between heaven and earth while they watched it, until they set it down with Ṭālūt; then they acknowledged his kingship and hastened to jihad, and he chose seventy thousand of their young men.

celaleyn:249-249.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ﴾ went out ﴿طَالُوتُ بِالْجُنُودِ﴾ from Bayt al-Maqdis — it was intensely hot and they asked him for water — ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُمْ﴾ will test you ﴿بِنَهَرٍ﴾ so that the obedient among you and the disobedient become manifest; it is between the Jordan and Palestine. ﴿فَمَنْ شَرِبَ مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of its water, ﴿فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي﴾ i.e. of my followers, ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَطْعَمْهُ﴾ taste it ﴿فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma [غَرْفَةً] ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾ and was content with it and did not exceed it — he is of me. ﴿فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ﴾ when they reached it, abundantly, ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ who confined themselves to the handful. It is narrated that it sufficed them for their drinking and their mounts, and they were three hundred and some ten-odd men. ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ هُوَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ — and they are those who confined themselves to the handful — ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. those who drank: ﴿لَا طَاقَةَ﴾ strength ﴿لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ﴾ i.e. to fight them; and they were cowardly and did not cross it. ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ﴾ are certain ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُوا اللَّهِ﴾ at the resurrection — and they are those who crossed it —: ﴿كَمْ﴾ declarative (khabariyya), in the sense of "many" ﴿مِنْ فِئَةٍ﴾ a group ﴿قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will; ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ with help and victory.
